title.zh: 卷一百三十六 列傳第六十一 李光弼附:荔非元禮 郝廷玉 李國臣 白孝德 張伯儀 白元光 陳利貞 侯仲莊 柏良器 烏承玼
title.en: Volume 136 Biographies 61: Li Guangbi Relations: Lifei Yuanli, Hao Tingyu, Li Guochen, Bai Xiaode, Zhang Boyi, Bai Yuanguang, Chen Lizhen, Hou Zhongzhuang, Bai Liangqi, Wu Chengci
title.raw: 卷一百三十六 列傳第六十一 李光弼附:荔非元禮 郝廷玉 李國臣 白孝德 張伯儀 白元光 陳利貞 侯仲莊 柏良器 烏承玼 Volume 136 Biographies 61: Li Guangbi Relations: Lifei Yuanli, Hao Tingyu, Li Guochen, Bai Xiaode, Zhang Boyi, Bai Yuanguang, Chen Lizhen, Hou Zhongzhuang, Bai Liangqi, Wu Chengci

sentences.zh: 李光弼子:彙 弟:光進 附:荔非元禮 郝廷玉 李國臣 白孝德 張伯儀 白元光 陳利貞 侯仲莊 柏良器 烏承玼

translations.literal: Li Guangbi's son: Hui; younger brother: Guangjin; appended biographies: Lifei Yuanli, Hao Tingyu, Li Guochen, Bai Xiaode, Zhang Boyi, Bai Yuanguang, Chen Lizhen, Hou Zhongzhuang, Bai Liangqi, Wu Chengci
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi — his son Hui; his younger brother Guangjin — with appended biographies of Lifei Yuanli, Hao Tingyu, Li Guochen, Bai Xiaode, Zhang Boyi, Bai Yuanguang, Chen Lizhen, Hou Zhongzhuang, Bai Liangqi, and Wu Chengci

sentences.zh: 李光弼

translations.literal: Li Guangbi
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi

sentences.zh: 李光弼，營州柳城人。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi was a man of Liucheng in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi was a native of Liucheng in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父楷洛，本契丹酋長，武后時入朝，累官左羽林大將軍，封薊郡公。

translations.literal: His father Kailuo was originally a Khitan chieftain; he entered the court in Empress Wu's time, rose through offices to Left General of the Feathered Forest, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kailuo had been a Khitan chieftain who came to court during Empress Wu's reign, rose through successive posts to Left General of the Feathered Forest, and was created Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇河源，楷洛率精兵擊走之。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans raided Heyuan, Kailuo led elite troops and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided Heyuan, Kailuo led picked troops and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 初行，謂人曰：「賊平，吾不歸矣。」

translations.literal: At the outset of the campaign he told others, "When the bandits are pacified, I shall not return.
translations.idiomatic: As he set out, he told those around him, "Once the enemy is crushed, I will not be coming home.

sentences.zh: 師還，卒於道，贈營州都督，諡曰忠烈。

translations.literal: The army returned; he died on the road. He was posthumously made Military Governor of Ying Prefecture, with the posthumous title Loyal and Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The army turned back, but he died on the march. He was posthumously appointed Military Governor of Ying Prefecture and given the posthumous name Loyal and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 光弼嚴毅沉果，有大略，幼不嬉弄，善騎射。

translations.literal: Guangbi was stern, resolute, deep, and decisive, with great strategic vision; in youth he did not play idly and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi was stern, resolute, and decisive, with a gift for grand strategy; even as a boy he shunned idle play and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 起家左衛親府左郎將，累遷左清道率，兼安北都護，補河西王忠嗣府兵馬使，充赤水軍使。

translations.literal: He began his career as Left Captain in the Left Guard's Personal Office, was promoted through posts to Left Commander of the Clear Way, concurrently Protector-General of the Pacified North, and was attached to Wang Zhongsi's Hexi headquarters as army horse commissioner, serving as commander of the Chishui Army.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a Left Captain in the Left Guard's Personal Office, rose through successive appointments to Left Commander of the Clear Way and concurrent Protector-General of the Pacified North, joined Wang Zhongsi's Hexi staff as army horse commissioner, and served as commander of the Chishui Army.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣遇之厚，雖宿將莫能比。

translations.literal: Zhongsi treated him generously; even veteran generals could not compare.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi favored him beyond what even his senior generals received.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「它日得我兵者，光弼也。」

translations.literal: He once said, "The one who will one day command my troops is Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked, "The man who will one day take command of my army is Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 俄襲父封。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he inherited his father's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he inherited his father's noble title.

sentences.zh: 以破吐蕃、吐谷渾功，進雲麾將軍。

translations.literal: For merit in defeating the Tibetans and Tuyuhun, he was promoted to Cloud-Banner General.
translations.idiomatic: For victories over the Tibetans and Tuyuhun, he was promoted to Cloud-Banner General.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使安思順表為副，知留後事，愛其材，欲以子妻之，光弼引疾去。

translations.literal: Shuofang Military Governor An Sishun memorialized him as deputy and acting regent; loving his talent, he wished to marry him to his son, but Guangbi pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: An Sishun, Military Governor of Shuofang, recommended him as deputy and acting regent. An admired his ability and wanted a son to marry Guangbi's daughter, but Guangbi pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度使哥舒翰異其操，表還長安。

translations.literal: Longyou Military Governor Geshu Han was struck by his character and memorialized for his return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, Military Governor of Longyou, was impressed by his conduct and had him recalled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，郭子儀薦其能，詔攝御史大夫，持節河東節度副大使，知節度事，兼雲中太守。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Guo Ziyi recommended his ability; he was ordered to act as Censor-in-Chief, to bear the staff as deputy military commissioner of Hedong with control of commission affairs, and concurrently as Prefect of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, Guo Ziyi commended his ability. An edict appointed him acting Censor-in-Chief, deputy military commissioner of Hedong with full control of the commission, and concurrent prefect of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 尋加魏郡太守、河北採訪使。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Prefect of Wei Commandery and Hebei Investigating Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also appointed prefect of Wei Commandery and investigating commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 光弼以朔方兵五千出土門，東救常山，次真定，常山團結子弟執賊將安思義降。

translations.literal: Guangbi led five thousand Shuofang troops out through Tumen Pass to relieve Changshan in the east, halted at Zhending, and the united youths of Changshan seized the rebel general An Siyi and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi marched five thousand Shuofang troops out through Tumen Pass to relieve Changshan in the east and encamped at Zhending, where local militia seized the rebel general An Siyi and surrendered him.

sentences.zh: 自顏杲卿死，郡為戰區，露胔蔽野，光弼酹而哭之，出為賊幽閉者，厚恤其家。

translations.literal: Since Yan Gaoqing's death the commandery had been a battle zone; exposed corpses covered the fields. Guangbi offered libations and wept, released those the rebels had imprisoned, and generously comforted their families.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yan Gaoqing's death the region had been a battleground, with unburied corpses strewn across the fields. Guangbi poured libations and wept over the dead, freed those the rebels had imprisoned, and gave their families generous relief.

sentences.zh: 時賊將史思明、李立節、蔡希德攻饒陽，光弼得思義，不殺，問其計，答曰：「今軍行疲勞，逢敵不可支，不如按軍入守，料勝而出。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel generals Shi Siming, Li Lijie, and Cai Xide were attacking Raoyang. Guangbi had captured Siyi but did not kill him; he asked his plan, and the answer was: "The army is now weary on the march and cannot stand against the enemy if met; better to hold the army in defense and strike only when victory is assured.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel generals Shi Siming, Li Lijie, and Cai Xide were then besieging Raoyang. Guangbi had taken Siyi alive and, instead of executing him, asked his counsel. Siyi replied, "Your troops are exhausted from the march and cannot stand a meeting engagement. Hold the city, wait until you can count on victory, then strike.

sentences.zh: 虜兵焱銳，弗能持重，圖之萬全。」

translations.literal: The barbarian troops blaze with keen edge; they cannot endure a prolonged standoff — plan for complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy are fierce and impetuous; they cannot keep up a prolonged standoff. That is the surest course.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 據城待。

translations.literal: He held the city and waited.
translations.idiomatic: He held the city and waited.

sentences.zh: 明日，思明兵二萬傅堞，光弼兵不得出，乃以勁弩五百射之，賊退，徙陣稍北。

translations.literal: The next day Siming's twenty thousand men pressed the ramparts; Guangbi's troops could not sally. He therefore used five hundred powerful crossbows to shoot them; the rebels withdrew and shifted their line somewhat north.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Siming brought twenty thousand men up to the walls. Unable to sortie, Guangbi deployed five hundred heavy crossbows and drove the rebels back, forcing them to shift their line northward.

sentences.zh: 光弼出其南，夾滹沱而軍。

translations.literal: Guangbi came out to their south and encamped flanking the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi marched out to their south and encamped with the Hutuo River at his flank.

sentences.zh: 思明雖數困，然恃近救，解鞍休士。

translations.literal: Though Siming had been repeatedly distressed, he relied on nearby relief and unslung saddles to rest his men.
translations.idiomatic: Though Siming had been hard pressed several times, he counted on reinforcements nearby and let his men dismount and rest.

sentences.zh: 是日，饒陽賊五千至九門，光弼諜知之，提輕兵，斂旗鼓，伺賊方飯，襲殺之且盡。

translations.literal: That day five thousand rebels from Raoyang reached Jiumen. Guangbi's scouts learned of it; he led light troops, stilled banners and drums, waited until the rebels were at their meal, and raided them, killing nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: That day five thousand rebels from Raoyang reached Jiumen. Guangbi's scouts reported it; he led light troops, muffled banners and drums, struck while the enemy were at their meal, and killed nearly every man.

sentences.zh: 思明懼，引去，以奇兵斷饟道。

translations.literal: Siming grew afraid and withdrew, sending picked troops to cut the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Siming, alarmed, pulled back and sent raiders to cut Guangbi's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 馬食薦藉，光弼命將取芻行唐，賊鈔擊之，兵負戶戰，賊不能奪。

translations.literal: The horses ate straw mats; Guangbi ordered generals to fetch fodder at Xingtang. The rebels raided them; the troops fought with doors on their backs, and the rebels could not seize it.
translations.idiomatic: With the horses reduced to eating straw mats, Guangbi sent officers to fetch fodder at Xingtang. Rebels intercepted them, but his men fought shielded by doors they carried on their backs, and the enemy could not wrest the supplies away.

sentences.zh: 會郭子儀收雲中，詔悉眾出井陘，與光弼合擊賊九門西，思明大敗，挺身走趙郡，立節中流矢死，希德走钜鹿。

translations.literal: When Guo Ziyi recovered Yunzhong, an edict ordered all forces out through Jingxing Pass to join Guangbi in striking the rebels west of Jiumen. Siming was greatly defeated, fled alone to Zhao Commandery; Lijie died of an arrow wound; Xide fled to Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi then recovered Yunzhong, and an edict ordered the full army through Jingxing Pass to join Guangbi in attacking the rebels west of Jiumen. Siming was routed and fled alone to Zhao; Lijie was killed by an arrow; Xide fled toward Julu.

sentences.zh: 收稿城等十縣，遂攻趙。

translations.literal: They recovered Gao City and nine other counties, then attacked Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered Gao City and nine other counties, then laid siege to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 詔加光弼范陽大都督府長史、范陽節度使。

translations.literal: An edict additionally appointed Guangbi Chief Secretary of the Fanyang Grand Protectorate and Military Governor of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Guangbi to chief secretary of the Fanyang Grand Protectorate and military governor of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 思明繇鼓城入博陵，殺官吏。

translations.literal: Siming entered Boling by way of Gucheng and killed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Siming entered Boling by way of Gucheng and slaughtered the local officials.

sentences.zh: 景城、河間、信都、清河、平原、博平六郡結營自守，以附光弼。

translations.literal: The six commanderies Jingcheng, Hejian, Xindu, Qinghe, Pingyuan, and Boping formed camps to defend themselves and attached themselves to Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Six commanderies — Jingcheng, Hejian, Xindu, Qinghe, Pingyuan, and Boping — raised local defenses and rallied to Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 光弼急攻趙，一日拔之。

translations.literal: Guangbi pressed the attack on Zhao and took it in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi pressed the siege of Zhao and captured it in a single day.

sentences.zh: 士多鹵掠，光弼坐譙門，收所獲，悉歸之民，城中大悅。

translations.literal: The soldiers plundered heavily; Guangbi sat at the watchtower gate, gathered what had been taken, and returned it all to the people; the city rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: His troops had looted freely, so Guangbi sat at the gate tower, collected everything taken, and returned it all to the townspeople. The city was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 進圍博陵，未下。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Boling but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to besiege Boling but could not bring it down.

sentences.zh: 與子儀合擊思明於嘉山，大破之。

translations.literal: Together with Ziyi he struck Siming at Jia Mountain and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Guo Ziyi, he met Siming at Jia Mountain and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 光弼以范陽本賊巢窟，當先取之，揠賊根本。

translations.literal: Guangbi held that Fanyang was originally the rebels' lair and should be taken first to uproot the enemy's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi argued that Fanyang, the rebels' original stronghold, must be taken first to cut their roots.

sentences.zh: 會潼關失守，乃拔軍入井陘。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass fell, he withdrew the army into Jingxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Pass fell, he withdrew his army through Jingxing Pass.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，詔以兵赴靈武，更授戶部尚書、同中書門下平章事，節度如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, an edict ordered troops to proceed to Lingwu; he was further appointed Minister of Revenue and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Chancellery, his commission unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne, an edict ordered Guangbi's army to Lingwu and appointed him Minister of Revenue and associate director of the Secretariat with the Chancellery, while retaining his military commission.

sentences.zh: 光弼以景城、河間兵五千入太原。

translations.literal: Guangbi led five thousand troops from Jingcheng and Hejian into Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi entered Taiyuan with five thousand troops from Jingcheng and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 前此，節度使王承業政弛謬，侍御史崔眾主兵太原，每侮狎承業，光弼素不平。

translations.literal: Before this, Military Governor Wang Chengye's government had been lax and mistaken; Supervising Censor Cui Zhong commanded troops at Taiyuan and constantly insulted and treated Chengye lightly; Guangbi had long been displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the military governor Wang Chengye had governed loosely and badly, while Supervising Censor Cui Zhong held real command at Taiyuan and routinely humiliated Chengye — a state of affairs Guangbi had long resented.

sentences.zh: 及是，詔眾以兵付光弼。

translations.literal: At this time an edict ordered Zhong to hand the troops to Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered Cui Zhong to transfer command to Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 眾素狂易，見光弼長揖，不即付兵，光弼怒，收系之。

translations.literal: Zhong was by nature arrogant and insolent; seeing Guangbi he made only a long bow and did not promptly hand over the troops. Guangbi grew angry and had him arrested and bound.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was habitually arrogant. He greeted Guangbi with nothing more than a casual bow and refused to hand over the troops at once. Guangbi had him arrested on the spot.

sentences.zh: 會使者至，拜眾御史中丞。

translations.literal: An envoy arrived and invested Zhong as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Just then an imperial messenger arrived to invest Zhong as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「眾有罪，已前系，今但斬侍御史。

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "Zhong is guilty and was already bound earlier; today I execute only the Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "Zhong is guilty and was already in custody. Today I execute only the Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 若使者宣詔，亦斬中丞。」

translations.literal: If the envoy proclaims the edict, I shall also execute the Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: If you proclaim the edict, I shall execute the Vice Censor-in-Chief as well.

sentences.zh: 使者內詔不敢出，乃斬眾以徇，威震三軍。

translations.literal: The envoy kept the edict inside and dared not produce it; Guangbi then executed Zhong as a warning, and awe shook the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger kept the edict hidden and dared not produce it. Guangbi executed Zhong before the ranks, and the whole army trembled at his authority.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，思明、希德率高秀岩、牛廷玠將兵十萬攻光弼。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, Siming and Xide, leading Gao Xiuyan and Niu Tingjie, brought a hundred thousand troops to attack Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide, Siming and Xide, with Gao Xiuyan and Niu Tingjie, led a hundred thousand men against Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 時銳兵悉赴朔方，而麾下卒不滿萬，眾議培城以守，光弼曰：「城環四十里，賊至治之，徒疲吾人。」

translations.literal: At that time the crack troops had all gone to Shuofang, and those under his banner were fewer than ten thousand. The assembly debated raising the walls to hold the city. Guangbi said, "The city wall runs forty li around; if we repair it when the enemy comes, we only weary our men.
translations.idiomatic: His best troops had all been sent to Shuofang, leaving fewer than ten thousand under his command. His officers urged strengthening the walls for a siege defense. Guangbi replied, "The walls run forty li around the city. Repairing them under enemy pressure would only exhaust our men.

sentences.zh: 乃徹民屋為摞石車，車二百人挽之，石所及輒數十人死，賊傷十二。

translations.literal: He therefore tore down houses to make stone-launching carts; two hundred men hauled each cart, and wherever the stones struck dozens died; the rebels suffered twelve thousand casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he demolished houses to build stone-throwing engines, each hauled by two hundred men. Wherever a stone landed, dozens of enemy fell; rebel casualties ran to twelve thousand.

sentences.zh: 思明為飛樓，障以木幔，築土山臨城，光弼遣穴地頹之。

translations.literal: Siming built flying towers screened with wooden curtains and piled an earthen hill against the city; Guangbi sent men to tunnel underground and topple it.
translations.idiomatic: Siming built assault towers screened with wooden curtains and raised an earthen mound against the walls. Guangbi countered by tunneling beneath it and collapsing the mound.

sentences.zh: 思明宴城下，倡優居臺上靳指天子，光弼遣人隧地禽取之。

translations.literal: Siming feasted below the city; entertainers on a platform pointed and mocked the Son of Heaven. Guangbi sent men through tunnels to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Siming held a feast below the walls while performers on a platform mocked the emperor. Guangbi sent men through the tunnels to seize them.

sentences.zh: 思明大駭，徙牙帳遠去，軍中皆視地後行。

translations.literal: Siming was greatly alarmed, moved his headquarters far away, and throughout the army men watched the ground as they walked.
translations.idiomatic: Siming was terrified, moved his headquarters far back, and ordered his men to watch the ground wherever they marched.

sentences.zh: 又潛溝營地，將沈其軍，乃陽約降。

translations.literal: He also secretly trenched the camp ground intending to flood the army, then openly agreed to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He also dug secret channels through the camp to flood Guangbi's position, then feigned willingness to surrender.

sentences.zh: 至期，以甲士守陴，遣裨校出，若送款者，思明大悅。

translations.literal: When the day came, armored men guarded the battlements while he sent a lieutenant out as if to offer submission; Siming was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day Guangbi lined armored men along the battlements and sent a lieutenant out as if to surrender. Siming was delighted.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊數千沒於塹，城上鼓噪，突騎出乘之，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: Soon several thousand rebels sank into the trench; drums and shouts rose on the wall, and shock cavalry sallied to take advantage, capturing and slaying on the order of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later thousands of rebels plunged into the flooded trenches. Drums thundered on the walls and shock cavalry burst out upon them, capturing and killing tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 思明畏敗，乃去，留希德攻太原。

translations.literal: Siming, fearing defeat, then withdrew, leaving Xide to attack Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Siming, fearing defeat, withdrew and left Xide to continue the siege of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 光弼出敢死士搏賊，斬首七萬級，希德委資糧遁走。

translations.literal: Guangbi sent dare-to-die troops to grapple the enemy, taking seventy thousand heads; Xide abandoned stores and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi sent his dare-to-die troops into the fight, claiming seventy thousand enemy heads. Xide abandoned his supplies and fled.

sentences.zh: 初，賊至，光弼設公幄城隅以止息，經府門不顧。

translations.literal: At first, when the rebels arrived, Guangbi set up a public tent at the corner of the wall to rest and passed the government gate without a glance.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first arrived, Guangbi pitched a field tent at the corner of the wall and slept there, passing his own headquarters without so much as a glance inside.

sentences.zh: 圍解，閱三昔乃歸私寢。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, only after three nights did he return to his private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Not until three nights after the siege lifted did he return to his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 收清夷、橫野等軍。

translations.literal: He recovered the Qingyi, Hengye, and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered the Qingyi, Hengye, and other scattered units.

sentences.zh: 賊別將攻好畤，破大橫關，光弼追敗之。

translations.literal: A rebel detached commander attacked Haochi, broke Daheng Pass, and Guangbi pursued and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel detached force attacked Haochi and broke through Daheng Pass; Guangbi pursued and routed them.

sentences.zh: 加檢校司徒，尋遷司空，封鄭國公，食實戶八百。

translations.literal: He was made Acting Minister of Works, soon transferred to Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng, with an income of eight hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Minister of Works, soon made full Minister of Works, created Duke of Zheng, and granted an income of eight hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，入朝，詔朝官四品以上郊謁，進兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan he entered court; an edict ordered officials of the fourth rank and above to greet him in the suburbs; he was advanced to concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan he came to court. An edict required officials of the fourth rank and above to greet him in the suburbs, and he was promoted to concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 與九節度圍安慶緒於相州，大戰鄴西，敗之。

translations.literal: With the nine military commissioners he besieged An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture and fought a great battle west of Ye, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Joining the nine military commissioners, he besieged An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture and won a great victory west of Ye.

sentences.zh: 光弼與諸將議：「思明勒兵魏州，欲以怠我，不如起軍逼之。

translations.literal: Guangbi discussed with the generals: "Siming is massing troops at Wei Prefecture intending to make us slack; better to raise the army and press him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi urged his generals, "Siming is holding troops at Wei Prefecture to lull us into complacency. We should march against him at once.

sentences.zh: 彼懲嘉山之敗，不敢輕出，則慶緒可禽。」

translations.literal: Chastened by defeat at Jia Mountain, he will not dare sally lightly; then Qingxu can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by his defeat at Jia Mountain, he will not dare march out lightly, and then we can take Qingxu.

sentences.zh: 觀軍容使魚朝恩固謂不可。

translations.literal: Army Supervising Commissioner Yu Chaoen obstinately said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Army Supervising Commissioner Yu Chaoen flatly refused.

sentences.zh: 既而思明來援，光弼拒賊，戰尤力，殺略大當。

translations.literal: Soon Siming came to relieve the siege; Guangbi blocked the rebels and fought with especial force, killing and capturing in great measure.
translations.idiomatic: Siming soon arrived with reinforcements. Guangbi met the rebels head-on, fought with exceptional ferocity, and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 會諸將驚潰，各引歸，所在剽掠，獨光弼整眾還太原。

translations.literal: When the generals panicked and broke, each led his men back, plundering wherever they went; Guangbi alone brought his forces back in order to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The allied generals then panicked and broke, each marching home and looting along the way. Guangbi alone brought his army back in good order to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝貸諸將罪，以光弼兼幽州大都督府長史，知諸道節度行營事。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned the generals' offenses and made Guangbi concurrent Chief Secretary of the Youzhou Grand Protectorate with control of all circuit military commissioners' field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned the other generals and appointed Guangbi concurrent chief secretary of the Youzhou Grand Protectorate with authority over all field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 又代子儀為朔方節度使。

translations.literal: He also replaced Ziyi as Military Governor of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He also replaced Guo Ziyi as military governor of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為天下兵馬副元帥。

translations.literal: Before long he became Deputy Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named deputy commander-in-chief of all forces under heaven.

sentences.zh: 光弼以河東騎五百馳東都，夜入其軍，且謂賊方窺洛，當扼虎牢，帥師東出河上。

translations.literal: Guangbi galloped to the Eastern Capital with five hundred Hedong cavalry, entered the army by night, and said the rebels were watching Luoyang and that they should hold Hulao Pass and lead the army east along the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi raced to the Eastern Capital with five hundred Hedong horsemen, entered camp at night, and declared that with the rebels eyeing Luoyang they must hold Hulao Pass and lead the army east along the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 檄召兵馬使張用濟，用濟憚光弼嚴，教諸將逗留其兵。

translations.literal: He summoned by dispatch the army horse commissioner Zhang Yongji; Yongji feared Guangbi's severity and instructed the generals to detain their troops.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Army Horse Commissioner Zhang Yongji by dispatch. Yongji, fearing Guangbi's severity, told the generals to hold their troops back.

sentences.zh: 用濟單騎入謁，光弼斬之，以辛京杲代。

translations.literal: Yongji came alone on horseback to an audience; Guangbi executed him and replaced him with Xin Jinggao.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji rode in alone to present himself. Guangbi had him executed and appointed Xin Jinggao in his place.

sentences.zh: 復追都將僕固懷恩，懷恩懼，先期至。

translations.literal: He again pursued the commandery general Pugu Huai'en; Huai'en was afraid and arrived ahead of time.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent for Commandery General Pugu Huai'en, who, terrified, arrived ahead of the summons.

sentences.zh: 會滑汴節度使許叔冀戰不利，降賊，思明乘勝西向。

translations.literal: When Huabian Military Governor Xu Shuji fought unsuccessfully and surrendered to the rebels, Siming rode his victory westward.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shuji, military governor of Huabian, was defeated and surrendered, Siming pressed his advantage westward.

sentences.zh: 光弼敦陣徐行，趨東京，謂留守韋陟曰：「賊新勝，難與爭鋒，欲詘之以計。

translations.literal: Guangbi tightened ranks and marched slowly toward the Eastern Capital, saying to the regent Wei Zhi, "The rebels have just won and are hard to meet in the edge; I wish to bend them by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi tightened his formation and advanced slowly toward the Eastern Capital. He told the regent Wei Zhi, "The rebels have just won and are not to be met head-on. I mean to wear them down by strategy.

sentences.zh: 然洛無見糧，危偪難守，公計安出？」

translations.literal: Yet Luoyang has no visible grain stores; pressed by danger it is hard to hold — what plan do you offer?
translations.idiomatic: But Luoyang has no grain in sight, and the danger is pressing. What is your counsel?

sentences.zh: 陟曰：「益陝兵，公保潼關，可以持久。」

translations.literal: Zhi said, "Increase the Shaanxi troops; you hold Tong Pass and can endure long."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhi replied, "Reinforce with troops from Shaanxi and hold Tong Pass. That way we can last."

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「兩軍相敵，尺寸地必爭。

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "When two armies face each other, every inch of ground must be contested.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "When two armies face each other, every foot of ground is contested.

sentences.zh: 今委五百里而守關，賊得地，勢益張。

translations.literal: Now to abandon five hundred li and merely hold the pass — the rebels gain territory and their momentum grows.
translations.idiomatic: If we yield five hundred li of territory and merely hold the pass, the rebels gain ground and their momentum only grows.

sentences.zh: 不如移軍河陽，北阻澤、潞，勝則出，敗則守，表裏相應，賊不得西，此猿臂勢也。

translations.literal: Better to shift the army to Heyang, blocking Ze and Lu to the north — victorious then sally, defeated then hold, inner and outer in mutual support so the rebels cannot go west; this is the ape-arm posture.
translations.idiomatic: Better to shift to Heyang, with Ze and Lu blocking the north. If we win, we advance; if we lose, we hold. Inner and outer positions will support each other, and the rebels cannot push west. That is the 'ape's arm' formation."

sentences.zh: 夫辨朝廷之禮，我不如公；

translations.literal: In discerning court ritual, I am not your equal;
translations.idiomatic: In matters of court ritual, I am no match for you;

sentences.zh: 論軍旅勝負，公不如我。」

translations.literal: in discussing victory and defeat in the army, you are not my equal."
translations.idiomatic: but in the calculus of victory and defeat on the battlefield, you are no match for me."

sentences.zh: 陟不能答。

translations.literal: Zhi could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhi had no answer.

sentences.zh: 判官韋損曰：「東都乃帝宅，公當守之。」

translations.literal: Judge Wei Sun said, "The Eastern Capital is the emperor's dwelling; you ought to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Wei Sun objected, "The Eastern Capital is the emperor's own city. You ought to defend it.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「汜水、崿嶺盡為賊蹊，子能盡守乎？」

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "Sishui and Eling are all rebel paths — can you guard them all?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi replied, "Every path through Sishui and Eling is open to the enemy. Can you guard them all?"

sentences.zh: 遂檄河南縱官吏避賊，閈無留人，督軍取戰守備。

translations.literal: He then issued a dispatch through Henan allowing officials to flee the rebels; no one was left in the lanes; he urged the army to take battle gear and defensive stores.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued orders through Henan allowing officials to flee the rebels, cleared the streets of civilians, and pressed his army to gather weapons and supplies for the coming fight.

sentences.zh: 思明至偃師，光弼悉軍趨河陽，身以五百騎殿。

translations.literal: When Siming reached Yanshi, Guangbi led the whole army toward Heyang, himself bringing up the rear with five hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Siming reached Yanshi, Guangbi marched his entire force toward Heyang, personally commanding five hundred horsemen as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 賊游騎至石橋，諸將曰：「並城而北乎？

translations.literal: Rebel scouts reached Shiqiao; the generals said, "Shall we go north along the city wall?
translations.idiomatic: Rebel scouts reached Shiqiao Bridge. His generals asked, "Shall we march north along the city wall?

sentences.zh: 當石橋進乎？」

translations.literal: Or advance by way of Shiqiao?
translations.idiomatic: Or cross at the bridge?

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「當石橋進。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "Advance by way of Shiqiao."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "Cross at the bridge."

sentences.zh: 夜甲，士持炬徐引，部曲重堅，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: At night they donned armor; the men carried torches and advanced slowly; the ranks were heavy and firm, and the rebels did not dare press.
translations.idiomatic: That night they donned armor. His men carried torches and advanced at a deliberate pace in tight formation, and the rebels did not dare close.

sentences.zh: 已入三城，眾二萬，軍才十日糧，與卒伍均少棄甘。

translations.literal: Having entered the three cities, the force was twenty thousand; the army had only ten days' grain; he shared scant sweets equally with the rank and file.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the three cities he had twenty thousand men and only ten days' rations. He shared what little sweets he had equally with the rank and file.

sentences.zh: 賊憚光弼，未敢犯宮闕，頓白馬祠，治塹溝，築月城以守。

translations.literal: The rebels feared Guangbi and did not dare assault the palace precincts; they halted at the White Horse Shrine, dug trenches and ditches, and built crescent ramparts to hold.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels feared Guangbi and did not dare assault the palace quarter. They encamped at the White Horse Shrine, dug trenches, and built crescent ramparts for a siege.

sentences.zh: 賊攻光弼，與戰中潬西，破逆黨，斬千級，溺死者甚眾，生執五千人。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked Guangbi; he fought them west of Zhongtan, broke the rebel party, beheaded a thousand, drowned very many, and captured five thousand alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked, he met them west of Zhongtan, routed their forces, beheaded a thousand, drowned a great many more, and took five thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 初，光弼謂李抱玉曰：「將軍能為我守南城二日乎？」

translations.literal: At first Guangbi said to Li Baoyu, "General, can you hold the south city for me for two days?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guangbi had asked Li Baoyu, "Can you hold the south city for me for two days?

sentences.zh: 抱玉曰：「過期何若？」

translations.literal: Baoyu said, "What if the time passes?"
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu asked, "What if I cannot hold it that long?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「棄之。」

translations.literal: He said, "Abandon it."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi replied, "Then abandon it."

sentences.zh: 抱玉許諾。

translations.literal: Baoyu promised.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu agreed.

sentences.zh: 即紿賊曰：「吾糧盡，明日當降。」

translations.literal: He immediately deceived the rebels, saying, "Our grain is exhausted; tomorrow we shall surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately deceived the enemy, announcing, "Our provisions are gone — we will surrender tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 賊喜，斂兵待期。

translations.literal: The rebels rejoiced and drew in their troops to await the day.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were delighted and held their troops back to await the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 抱玉已繕完，即請戰。

translations.literal: Baoyu had already finished repairs and immediately requested battle.
translations.idiomatic: Once his defenses were ready, Baoyu demanded battle at once.

sentences.zh: 賊忿欺，急攻之。

translations.literal: The rebels, angry at being deceived, pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Furious at being tricked, the rebels attacked in force.

sentences.zh: 抱玉出奇兵夾擊，俘獲過當，賊帥周摯引卻。

translations.literal: Baoyu sent picked troops to strike from both sides; captures exceeded the norm; the rebel commander Zhou Zhi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu sent raiders to strike from both flanks, taking prisoners beyond count. The rebel commander Zhou Zhi pulled back.

sentences.zh: 光弼自將治中潬，樹壁掘塹。

translations.literal: Guangbi personally led work on Zhongtan, building ramparts and digging trenches.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi personally directed the fortification of Zhongtan, building walls and digging trenches.

sentences.zh: 摯舍南城攻中潬，光弼遣荔非元禮戰羊馬，賊大潰。

translations.literal: Zhi abandoned the south city to attack Zhongtan; Guangbi sent Lifei Yuanli to fight at Yangma; the rebels were routed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi abandoned the south city to assault Zhongtan. Guangbi sent Lifei Yuanli to meet him at Yangma and routed the rebel army.

sentences.zh: 摯收兵復振，與安太清合眾三萬攻北城。

translations.literal: Zhi gathered his troops and revived their spirit; with An Taiqing he united thirty thousand men to attack the north city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi regrouped and, joining An Taiqing, massed thirty thousand men to assault the north city.

sentences.zh: 光弼斂軍入，登陴望曰：「彼軍雖銳，然方陣而囂，不足虞也，日中當破。」

translations.literal: Guangbi drew the army in, mounted the battlements to look, and said, "Their army is keen, yet they stand in square formation and are arrogant — not to be feared; at midday they will be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi drew his troops inside the walls, mounted the battlements, and said, "Their army is fierce, but they stand in rigid formation and are overconfident. They are nothing to fear — by midday they will break.

sentences.zh: 乃出戰，及期未決，召諸將曰：「彼強而可破者，亂也。

translations.literal: He then sallied; when the appointed time passed without decision, he summoned the generals and said, "What makes the strong breakable is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He sallied forth, but when midday passed without a decision he called his generals and said, "What makes a strong enemy beatable is disorder.

sentences.zh: 今以亂擊亂，宜無功。」

translations.literal: Now to strike disorder with disorder should yield no merit."
translations.idiomatic: Fighting disorder with disorder will get us nowhere."

sentences.zh: 因問：「賊陣何所最堅？」

translations.literal: He then asked, "Where is the enemy line strongest?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "Where is the enemy line strongest?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「西北隅。」

translations.literal: The answer was, "The northwest corner."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The northwest corner."

sentences.zh: 召郝廷玉曰：「為我以麾下破之。」

translations.literal: He summoned Hao Tingyu and said, "Break it for me under my banner."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Hao Tingyu. "Break it for me under my banner."

sentences.zh: 曰：「廷玉所將步卒，請騎五百。」

translations.literal: Tingyu said, "The foot soldiers I command — I request five hundred cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu said, "I command foot soldiers — give me five hundred horsemen."

sentences.zh: 與之三百。

translations.literal: He gave him three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi gave him three hundred.

sentences.zh: 復問其次，曰：「東南隅。」

translations.literal: He asked again for the next strongest; the answer was, "The southeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: He asked where the line was next strongest. "The southeast corner," came the reply.

sentences.zh: 召論惟貞，辭曰：「蕃將也，不知步戰，請鐵騎三百。」

translations.literal: He summoned Lun Weizhen, who declined, saying, "I am a barbarian general and do not know foot combat; I request three hundred iron cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Lun Weizhen, who protested, "I am a frontier officer and know nothing of infantry fighting — give me three hundred armored horsemen."

sentences.zh: 與之二百。

translations.literal: He gave him two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi gave him two hundred.

sentences.zh: 乃出賜馬四十，分給廷玉等。

translations.literal: He then brought out forty bestowed horses and divided them among Tingyu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought out forty imperial horses and distributed them among Tingyu and the others.

sentences.zh: 光弼執大旗曰：「望吾旗，麾若緩，可觀便宜。

translations.literal: Guangbi grasped the great banner and said, "Watch my flag; if the signal is slow, you may judge opportunity as you see fit.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi seized the command banner and said, "Watch my flag. If the signal is slow, use your own judgment.

sentences.zh: 若三麾至地，諸軍畢入，生死以之，退者斬！」

translations.literal: If the banner is waved to the ground three times, all armies enter together; stake life on it — whoever retreats is beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: When I lower the banner three times, every unit charges in together. Stake your lives on it — anyone who retreats will be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 既而馮堞望廷玉軍不能前，趣左右取其首來。

translations.literal: Soon, mounting the ramparts, he saw Tingyu's army could not advance and urged his attendants to bring Tingyu's head.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he mounted the ramparts and saw Tingyu's troops stalled. He ordered his attendants to bring him Tingyu's head.

sentences.zh: 廷玉曰：「馬中矢，非卻也。」

translations.literal: Tingyu said, "My horse was struck by an arrow; this is not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu called back, "My horse was hit — I am not retreating.

sentences.zh: 乃命易佗馬。

translations.literal: He then ordered another horse.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a fresh mount.

sentences.zh: 有裨將援矛刺賊，洞馬腹，中數人，又有迎賊不戰而卻者，光弼召援矛者賜絹五百匹，不戰者斬。

translations.literal: A lieutenant thrust with a spear at the rebels, piercing a horse's belly and striking several men; another met the rebels and withdrew without fighting. Guangbi summoned the spear-thruster and bestowed five hundred bolts of silk; the one who would not fight was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: One lieutenant drove his spear into the enemy ranks, piercing a horse's belly and striking several men. Another met the enemy and fell back without fighting. Guangbi rewarded the spearman with five hundred bolts of silk and beheaded the coward.

sentences.zh: 光弼麾旗三，諸軍爭奮，賊眾奔敗，斬首萬餘級，俘八千餘人，馬二千，軍資器械以億計，禽周摯、徐璜玉、李秦授，惟太清挺身走。

translations.literal: Guangbi waved the banner three times; all armies strove forward; the rebel masses fled in defeat; more than ten thousand heads were taken, over eight thousand captured, two thousand horses, military stores and weapons counted in the hundreds of millions; Zhou Zhi, Xu Huangyu, and Li Qinshou were seized; only Taiqing fled alone.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi lowered his banner three times and every unit charged. The rebels broke and fled. More than ten thousand were beheaded, over eight thousand captured, two thousand horses taken, and military stores beyond counting. Zhou Zhi, Xu Huangyu, and Li Qinshou were captured; only Taiqing escaped alone.

sentences.zh: 思明未知，猶攻南城，光弼驅所俘示之，思明大懼，築壘以拒官軍。

translations.literal: Siming did not yet know and still attacked the south city; Guangbi drove the captives forward to show them; Siming was greatly afraid and built ramparts to block the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Siming, still unaware, continued attacking the south city. Guangbi paraded his prisoners before the rebel lines. Siming was terrified and threw up fortifications to block the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 始，光弼將戰，內刀於靴，曰：「戰，危事。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Guangbi was about to fight, he hid a knife in his boot and said, "Battle is a perilous affair.
translations.idiomatic: Before the battle Guangbi had slipped a knife into his boot and said, "War is a perilous business.

sentences.zh: 吾位三公，不可辱於賊。

translations.literal: I hold the rank of the Three Dukes and cannot be shamed by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: I hold one of the three highest ranks in the realm and cannot suffer disgrace at rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 萬有一不捷，當自刎以謝天子。」

translations.literal: If by any chance we do not prevail, I shall cut my own throat to answer to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If fortune turns against us, I will cut my own throat to answer to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及是，西向拜舞，三軍感動。

translations.literal: At this time he bowed and danced rites facing west; the three armies were moved.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory he bowed toward the west in homage to the throne, and the whole army was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 太清襲懷州，守之。

translations.literal: Taiqing raided Huaizhou and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing seized Huaizhou and held it against the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，加太尉、中書令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan he was made Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan he was promoted to Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 進圍懷州，思明來救，光弼再逐北。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Huaizhou; Siming came to relieve it; Guangbi twice drove him north.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to besiege Huaizhou. When Siming came to relieve the city, Guangbi twice drove him back.

sentences.zh: 思明見兵河清，聲度河絕餉路。

translations.literal: Siming displayed troops at Heqing and proclaimed he would cross the river to cut the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Siming massed troops at Heqing and announced he would cross the river to cut Guangbi's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 光弼壁野水度，既夕還軍，留牙將雍希顥守，曰：「賊將高暉、李日越，萬人敵也，賊必使劫我。

translations.literal: Guangbi encamped at Yeshui Ford; at evening he returned the army but left Lieutenant-General Yong Xixian to hold the place, saying, "The rebel generals Gao Hui and Li Yueyue are match for ten thousand; the rebels are sure to send them to raid us.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi encamped at Yeshui Ford, then withdrew his main force at dusk, leaving Lieutenant-General Yong Xixian behind. "The rebel generals Gao Hui and Li Yueyue are worth ten thousand men each," he said. "Siming is sure to send them to raid this camp.

sentences.zh: 爾留此，賊至勿與戰，若降，與偕來。」

translations.literal: You stay here; when the rebels come do not fight them; if they surrender, bring them with you.
translations.idiomatic: Stay here. If they come, do not fight. If they wish to surrender, bring them to me.

sentences.zh: 左右竊怪語無倫。

translations.literal: Those at his side privately marveled that his words were without reason.
translations.idiomatic: His officers privately thought his orders made no sense.

sentences.zh: 是日，思明果召日越曰：「光弼野次，爾以鐵騎五百夜取之，不然，無歸！」

translations.literal: That day Siming indeed summoned Yueyue and said, "Guangbi is encamped in the open; you take five hundred iron cavalry and seize him by night — otherwise do not return!
translations.idiomatic: That same day Siming summoned Yueyue and said, "Guangbi is camped in the open. Take five hundred armored horsemen and seize him tonight — or do not come back!

sentences.zh: 日越至壘，使人問曰：「太尉在乎？」

translations.literal: Yueyue reached the ramparts and sent a man to ask, "Is the Grand Marshal here?"
translations.idiomatic: Yueyue reached the camp and sent a messenger to ask, "Is the Grand Marshal here?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「去矣。」

translations.literal: The answer was, "He has gone."
translations.idiomatic: The reply came, "He has already left."

sentences.zh: 「兵幾何？」

translations.literal: How many troops?"
translations.idiomatic: How many troops remain?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「千人。」

translations.literal: The answer was, "A thousand."
translations.idiomatic: A thousand."

sentences.zh: 「將為誰？」

translations.literal: Who commands?"
translations.idiomatic: Who commands them?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「雍希顥。」

translations.literal: The answer was, "Yong Xixian."
translations.idiomatic: Yong Xixian."

sentences.zh: 日越謂其下曰：「我受命雲何，今顧獲希顥，歸不免死。」

translations.literal: Yueyue said to his men, "What was I ordered to do? Now if I merely capture Xixian, returning I cannot escape death."
translations.idiomatic: Yueyue told his men, "What was I ordered to do? If I return having captured only Xixian, I am a dead man."

sentences.zh: 遂請降。

translations.literal: He then requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 希顥與俱至，光弼厚待之，表授特進，兼金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Xixian came with him; Guangbi treated him generously and memorialized him as specially advanced and concurrent Grand General of the Golden Crow.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian brought him in. Guangbi received him generously and recommended him for special advancement and appointment as Grand General of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 高暉聞，亦降。

translations.literal: When Gao Hui heard of it, he too surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Hui heard of this, he surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 或問：「公降二將何易也？」

translations.literal: Someone asked, "How did you so easily secure the surrender of these two generals?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "How did you secure the surrender of those two generals so easily?

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「思明再敗，恨不得野戰，聞我野次，彼固易之，命將來襲，必許以死。

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "Siming has been defeated twice and longs for a field battle; hearing I am encamped in the open, they naturally take it lightly and order generals to raid — surely promising death on failure.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi replied, "Siming has been defeated twice and is desperate for a field battle. Hearing that I was camped in the open, he naturally underestimated me and sent generals to raid us — on pain of death if they failed.

sentences.zh: 希顥無名，不足以為功。

translations.literal: Xixian has no fame and is not enough to count as merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian is nobody — capturing him would not count as a victory.

sentences.zh: 日越懼死，不降何待？

translations.literal: Yueyue feared death — if not surrender, what was he waiting for?
translations.idiomatic: Yueyue feared for his life — what else could he do but surrender?

sentences.zh: 高暉材出日越之右，降者見遇，貳者得不思奮乎？」

translations.literal: Gao Hui's talent surpasses Yueyue's; when those who surrender are well treated, will the doubtful not consider striving?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hui outranks Yueyue in ability. When defectors are rewarded so well, who among the wavering would not reconsider his loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 諸軍決丹水灌懷州，未下。

translations.literal: The armies dammed the Danshui to flood Huaizhou but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies dammed the Danshui to flood Huaizhou, but the city still held.

sentences.zh: 光弼令廷玉由地道入，得其軍號，登陴大呼，王師乘城，禽太清、楊希仲，送之京師，獻俘太廟。

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered Tingyu to enter by tunnel, learn the army signals, mount the battlements and shout; the imperial army scaled the wall, seized Taiqing and Yang Xizhong, sent them to the capital, and presented captives at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi sent Tingyu through a tunnel to learn the enemy's watchwords, then had him mount the walls and shout. The imperial troops scaled the city, captured Taiqing and Yang Xizhong, sent them to the capital, and presented the prisoners at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 進食實戶一千五百。

translations.literal: His income was advanced by fifteen hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: His income was increased by fifteen hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 思明使諜宣言賊將士皆北人，謳吟思歸。

translations.literal: Siming sent spies to proclaim that the rebel officers and soldiers were all northerners, singing and longing to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Siming planted agents to spread word that his troops were all northerners who sang of home and longed to return.

sentences.zh: 朝恩信然，屢上賊可滅狀。

translations.literal: Chaoen believed it and repeatedly submitted memorials that the rebels could be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chaoen believed them and repeatedly memorialized that the rebels could be destroyed at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 詔諭光弼，光弼固言賊方銳，未可輕動。

translations.literal: An edict instructed Guangbi; Guangbi firmly said the rebels were still keen and could not be lightly stirred.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent orders to Guangbi, but Guangbi insisted the rebels were still formidable and must not be provoked lightly.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩媢光弼功，陰佐朝恩陳掃除計。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en envied Guangbi's merit and secretly aided Chaoen in presenting plans for a sweeping purge.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en, jealous of Guangbi's achievements, secretly encouraged Chaoen's plans for a decisive offensive.

sentences.zh: 使者來督戰，光弼不得已，令李抱玉守河陽，出師次北邙。

translations.literal: Envoys came to press for battle; Guangbi had no choice; he ordered Li Baoyu to hold Heyang and led the army to encamp at North Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys arrived to demand battle. Guangbi had no choice. He left Li Baoyu to hold Heyang and marched out to encamp at North Mang.

sentences.zh: 光弼使傅山陣，懷恩曰：「我用騎，今迫險，非便地，請陣諸原。」

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered formation on Fu Mountain; Huai'en said, "I use cavalry; now pressed into difficult ground this is not favorable terrain — I request formation on the plains.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi drew up his line on Fu Mountain. Huai'en objected, "I fight with cavalry. This cramped ground is no place for horsemen — let us deploy on the open plain.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「有險，可以勝，可以敗；

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "With difficult ground one can win and one can lose;
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi replied, "Difficult ground can win a battle or lose one;

sentences.zh: 陣于原，敗斯殲矣。

translations.literal: arrayed on the plain, defeat means annihilation.
translations.idiomatic: but on open ground, defeat means annihilation.

sentences.zh: 且賊致死於我，不如阻險。」

translations.literal: Moreover the rebels will fight to the death against us — better to use difficult ground as a barrier."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels will fight to the death against us. Better to use the terrain as our shield.

sentences.zh: 懷恩不從。

translations.literal: Huai'en would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 賊據高原，以長戟七百，壯士執刀隨之，委物偽遁。

translations.literal: The rebels held the high ground, with seven hundred long halberds and strong men with blades following, abandoning goods in a feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the high ground with seven hundred pikemen and swordsmen in support, then feigned retreat, abandoning goods along the way.

sentences.zh: 懷恩軍爭剽獲，伏兵發，官軍大潰。

translations.literal: Huai'en's army scrambled to plunder; ambush troops sprang forth; the imperial army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's men scrambled to seize the abandoned goods. Ambush troops sprang up and the imperial army was routed.

sentences.zh: 懷州復陷，光弼度河保聞喜，抱玉以兵寡，棄河陽。

translations.literal: Huaizhou fell again; Guangbi crossed the river to hold Wensi; Baoyu, with few troops, abandoned Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhou fell again. Guangbi crossed the river to hold Wensi, while Baoyu, too weak to defend Heyang, abandoned the city.

sentences.zh: 光弼請罪，帝以懷恩違令覆軍，優詔召光弼入朝。

translations.literal: Guangbi requested punishment; the emperor, holding that Huai'en had disobeyed orders and destroyed the army, issued a gracious edict summoning Guangbi to court.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi submitted a confession of failure. The emperor blamed Huai'en for disobeying orders and ruining the army, and issued a gracious summons for Guangbi to come to court.

sentences.zh: 懇讓太尉，更拜開府儀同三司、中書令、河中尹、晉絳等州節度使。

translations.literal: He earnestly declined the Grand Marshal rank and was instead appointed Grand Master with Golden Document Equal to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Secretariat, Prefect of Hezhong, and Military Governor of Jin and Jiang and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly declined the rank of Grand Marshal and was instead appointed Grand Master with Golden Document Equal to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Secretariat, prefect of Hezhong, and military governor of Jin, Jiang, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復拜太尉，兼侍中、河南副元帥，知河南、淮南東西、山南東、荊南五道節度行營事，鎮泗州。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Grand Marshal, concurrent Palace Attendant, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Henan, with control of field headquarters for the five circuits Henan, Eastern and Western Huainan, Eastern Shannan, and Jingnan, stationed at Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again named Grand Marshal and concurrent Palace Attendant, deputy commander-in-chief of Henan with authority over field headquarters in five circuits — Henan, Eastern and Western Huainan, Eastern Shannan, and Jingnan — and stationed at Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝為賦詩以餞。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a poem to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed a poem to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 朝義乘邙山之捷，進略申、光等十三州，光弼輿疾就道，監軍使以兵少，請保揚州。

translations.literal: Chaoyi took advantage of his victory at Mangshan and advanced to seize Shen, Guang, and thirteen other prefectures. Guangbi, carried in a litter because of illness, set out on the road; the army supervisor, because the troops were few, requested that they defend Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi took advantage of his victory at Mangshan and advanced to seize Shen, Guang, and thirteen other prefectures. Guangbi, carried in a litter because of illness, set out on the road; the army supervisor, because the troops were few, requested that they defend Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「朝廷以安危寄我，賊安知吾眾寡？若出不意，當自潰。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said, “The court has entrusted its safety or danger to me. How can the rebels know whether my troops are many or few? If we appear unexpectedly, they will naturally collapse.”
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, “The court has entrusted its safety or danger to me. How can the rebels know whether my troops are many or few? If we appear unexpectedly, they will naturally collapse.”

sentences.zh: 遂疾驅入徐州。

translations.literal: He then drove swiftly into Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove swiftly into Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時朝義圍李岑于宋州，使田神功擊走之。

translations.literal: At that time Chaoyi had besieged Li Cen at Songzhou, and Guangbi sent Tian Shengong to attack and drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chaoyi had besieged Li Cen at Songzhou, and Guangbi sent Tian Shengong to attack and drive him off.

sentences.zh: 初，神功平劉展，逗留淮南，尚衡、殷仲卿相攻兗、鄆間，來瑱擅襄陽，及光弼至屯，朝義走，神功還河南，瑱、衡、仲卿踵入朝，其為諸將憚服類此。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Shengong pacified Liu Zhan, he lingered in Huainan; Shang Heng and Yin Zhongqing attacked one another between Yan and Yun, and Lai Tian occupied Xiangyang without authorization. When Guangbi arrived and encamped, Chaoyi fled, Shengong returned to Henan, and Tian, Heng, and Zhongqing followed one another into court. This was the sort of awe and submission he inspired in the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Shengong pacified Liu Zhan, he lingered in Huainan; Shang Heng and Yin Zhongqing attacked one another between Yan and Yun, and Lai Tian occupied Xiangyang without authorization. When Guangbi arrived and encamped, Chaoyi fled, Shengong returned to Henan, and Tian, Heng, and Zhongqing followed one another into court. This was the sort of awe and submission he inspired in the generals.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，進封臨淮郡王。

translations.literal: In Baoying 1, he was advanced in enfeoffment as Prince of Linhuai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1, he was advanced in enfeoffment as Prince of Linhuai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 光弼收許州，斬賊贏千級，縛偽將二十二人。

translations.literal: Guangbi recovered Xuzhou, beheaded more than a thousand rebels, and bound twenty-two false generals.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi recovered Xuzhou, beheaded more than a thousand rebels, and bound twenty-two false generals.

sentences.zh: 朝義分兵攻宋州，光弼破走之。

translations.literal: Chaoyi divided off troops to attack Songzhou, and Guangbi defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi divided off troops to attack Songzhou, and Guangbi defeated and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 浙東賊袁晁反台州，建元寶勝，以建醜為正月，殘剽州縣。

translations.literal: The eastern Zhejiang rebel Yuan Chao rose in rebellion at Taizhou, established the era Baosheng, made the month jianchou the first month, and ravaged and plundered prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Zhejiang rebel Yuan Chao rose in rebellion at Taizhou, established the era Baosheng, made the month jianchou the first month, and ravaged and plundered prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 光弼遣麾下破其眾於衢州。

translations.literal: Guangbi sent his subordinates to defeat his forces at Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi sent his subordinates to defeat his forces at Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，遂禽晁，浙東平。

translations.literal: In Guangde 1, Chao was finally captured, and eastern Zhejiang was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 1, Chao was finally captured, and eastern Zhejiang was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔增實封戶二千，與一子三品階，賜鐵券，名藏太廟，圖形淩煙閣。

translations.literal: An edict increased Guangbi’s substantive fief by two thousand households, granted one of his sons third-rank status, bestowed an iron certificate, stored his name in the imperial ancestral temple, and had his portrait painted in Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict increased Guangbi’s substantive fief by two thousand households, granted one of his sons third-rank status, bestowed an iron certificate, stored his name in the imperial ancestral temple, and had his portrait painted in Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 相州、北邙之敗，朝恩羞其策繆，故深忌光弼切骨，而程元振尤疾之。

translations.literal: After the defeats at Xiang Prefecture and North Mang, Chaoen was ashamed that his strategy had erred and therefore hated Guangbi to the bone; Cheng Yuanzhen especially detested him.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeats at Xiang and North Mang, Yu Chaoen was ashamed of his own bad counsel and came to hate Guangbi with a personal bitterness; Cheng Yuanzhen detested him even more.

sentences.zh: 二人用事，日謀有以中傷者。

translations.literal: The two held power and daily plotted means to wound him.
translations.idiomatic: With both men in power, they plotted daily to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 及來瑱為元振讒死，光弼愈恐。

translations.literal: When Lai Tian was slandered to death by Yuanzhen, Guangbi grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Tian was slandered to death by Yuanzhen, Guangbi's fear deepened.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇京師，代宗詔入援，光弼畏禍，遷延不敢行。

translations.literal: When Tibetans raided the capital region, Emperor Daizong ordered him to enter and relieve; Guangbi feared disaster and delayed, not daring to march.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans threatened the capital, Emperor Daizong ordered him to march to the relief. Guangbi, fearing a trap, delayed and would not move.

sentences.zh: 及帝幸陝，猶倚以為重，數存問其母，以解嫌疑。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Shan, he still relied on him as weighty and repeatedly inquired after his mother to dispel suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the emperor fled to Shan, he still counted on Guangbi's prestige and repeatedly sent inquiries after his mother to dispel suspicion.

sentences.zh: 帝還長安，因拜東都留守，察其去就。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to Chang'an, he appointed him regent of the Eastern Capital to observe his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Chang'an, he appointed Guangbi regent of the Eastern Capital to test his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 光弼以久須詔書不至，歸徐州收租賦為解。

translations.literal: Guangbi, because he had long awaited an edict that did not come, returned to Xuzhou to collect rents and taxes as his excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi, having waited in vain for further orders, returned to Xuzhou on the pretext of collecting taxes and tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝令郭子儀自河中輦其母還京。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Guo Ziyi from Hezhong to convey his mother back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Guo Ziyi to bring Guangbi's mother from Hezhong back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二年，光弼疾篤，奉表上前後所賜實封，詔不許。

translations.literal: In the second year Guangbi's illness was grave; he submitted a memorial offering back all the taxable households bestowed before and after; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of his appointment his illness grew grave. He submitted a memorial offering to return all the taxable households the throne had bestowed on him. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 將吏問後事，答曰：「吾淹軍中，不得就養，為不孝子，尚何言哉！」

translations.literal: Officers and clerks asked about affairs after his death; he answered, "I have lingered in the army and could not go home to support my parents — I am an unfilial son; what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: When his officers asked about his final wishes, he replied, "I have spent my life in the army and could not care for my parents at home. I am an unfilial son — what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 取所餘絹布分遺部將。

translations.literal: He took the remaining silk and cloth and distributed it among the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his remaining silk and cloth among his commanders.

sentences.zh: 薨，年五十七。

translations.literal: He died; age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 部將即以其布遂為光弼行喪，號哭相問。

translations.literal: The commanders immediately used that cloth to conduct mourning rites for Guangbi, wailing and inquiring of one another.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders immediately used that cloth to conduct his funeral rites, wailing and comforting one another.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使吊恤其母，贈太保，諡曰武穆，詔百官送葬延平門外。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to condole and comfort his mother; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian, with the posthumous title Martial and Solemn; an edict ordered all officials to escort the funeral outside Yanping Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to comfort his mother, posthumously appointed him Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Martial and Solemn, and ordered all officials to escort the funeral procession out through Yanping Gate.

sentences.zh: 光弼用兵，謀定而後戰，能以少覆眾。

translations.literal: In employing troops Guangbi settled plans before fighting and could with few overturn many.
translations.idiomatic: In warfare Guangbi planned thoroughly before he fought and could defeat larger forces with smaller ones.

sentences.zh: 治師訓整，天下服其威名，軍中指顧，諸將不敢仰視。

translations.literal: He governed the army with strict training; all under heaven submitted to his awe-inspiring name; in the army at a gesture or glance the generals did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled his troops to exacting discipline. All under heaven respected his authority; in camp a glance from him was enough to make his generals lower their eyes.

sentences.zh: 初，與郭子儀齊名，世稱「李郭」，而戰功推為中興第一。

translations.literal: At first he was famed equal to Guo Ziyi; the age called them "Li and Guo," yet in battle merit he was ranked first in the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been ranked equal to Guo Ziyi, and the age spoke of "Li and Guo" — yet in battle merit he was considered foremost among those who restored the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 其代子儀朔方也，營壘、士卒、麾幟無所更，而光弼一號令之，氣色乃益精明雲。

translations.literal: When he replaced Ziyi in Shuofang, camps, soldiers, and banners were unchanged; yet at Guangbi's single command their spirit grew still keener.
translations.idiomatic: When he replaced Guo Ziyi in Shuofang, the camps, troops, and banners were unchanged — yet a single command from Guangbi made the whole army's bearing grow sharper still.

sentences.zh: 子 彙

translations.literal: Son: Hui
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui

sentences.zh: 子彙，有志操，廉介自將。

translations.literal: His son Hui had aspiration and integrity, conducting himself with stern frugality.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui was a man of principle who conducted himself with austere integrity.

sentences.zh: 從賈耽為裨將，奏兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Following Jia Dan as a lieutenant general, he was memorialized as concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Jia Dan as a lieutenant general, he was recommended for concurrent appointment as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 元和初，分徐州苻離為宿州，光弼有遺愛，擢彙為刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era, Fuli of Xuzhou was split off as Suzhou; Guangbi had left behind beloved memory, and Hui was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanhe reign, Fuli was carved out of Xuzhou to form Suzhou. Because the people still cherished Li Guangbi's memory, Hui was promoted to prefect of the new prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後遷涇原節度使，罷軍中雜徭，出奉錢贖將士質賣子，還其家。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred as Military Governor of Jingyuan; he abolished miscellaneous corvée in the army, spent his salary to redeem officers and soldiers' children who had been pawned, and returned them to their families.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made military governor of Jingyuan. There he abolished miscellaneous corvée duties in the army and spent his own salary to redeem officers' and soldiers' children who had been sold into pawn, returning them to their families.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 光弼弟光進，字太應。

translations.literal: Guangbi’s younger brother Guangjin had the courtesy name Taiying.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi’s younger brother Guangjin had the courtesy name Taiying.

sentences.zh: 初為房琯裨將，將北軍戰陳濤斜，兵敗，奔行在，肅宗宥之。

translations.literal: At first he was a lieutenant general under Fang Guan and commanded the northern army in battle at Chentaoxie. When the army was defeated, he fled to the temporary imperial residence, and Suzong pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a lieutenant general under Fang Guan and commanded the northern army in battle at Chentaoxie. When the army was defeated, he fled to the temporary imperial residence, and Suzong pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，拜檢校太子太保，封涼國公。

translations.literal: When Daizong took the throne, Guangjin was appointed acting Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong took the throne, Guangjin was appointed acting Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃入寇，至便橋，郭子儀為副元帥，光進及郭英乂佐之。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans invaded and reached Bian Bridge, Guo Ziyi served as deputy commander-in-chief, and Guangjin and Guo Ying’ai assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans invaded and reached Bian Bridge, Guo Ziyi served as deputy commander-in-chief, and Guangjin and Guo Ying’ai assisted him.

sentences.zh: 自至德後與李輔國並掌禁兵，委以心膂。

translations.literal: After the Zhide era, he and Li Fuguo together commanded the palace troops and were trusted as intimate aides.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide era, he and Li Fuguo together commanded the palace troops and were trusted as intimate aides.

sentences.zh: 光弼被譖，出為渭北、邠甯節度使。

translations.literal: When Guangbi was slandered, Guangjin was sent out as military governor of Weibei and Binning.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi was slandered, Guangjin was sent out as military governor of Weibei and Binning.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，封武威郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongtai, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子太保，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and died.

sentences.zh: 母李，有須數十，長五寸許，封韓國太夫人，二子節制皆一品。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Li had several dozen whiskers, about five inches long. She was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Han, and both her sons held military governorships with first-rank status.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Li had several dozen whiskers, about five inches long. She was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Han, and both her sons held military governorships with first-rank status.

sentences.zh: 死葬長安南原，將相奠祭凡四十四幄，時以為榮。

translations.literal: When she died, she was buried on the southern plain of Chang’an; generals and ministers set up forty-four mourning tents for offerings, and people of the time considered it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, she was buried on the southern plain of Chang’an; generals and ministers set up forty-four mourning tents for offerings, and people of the time considered it an honor.

sentences.zh: 光弼所部將李懷光、僕固懷恩、田神功、李抱玉、董秦、哥舒曜、韓遊環、渾釋之、辛京杲自有傳。

translations.literal: Guangbi's subordinate generals Li Huai'guang, Pugu Huai'en, Tian Shegong, Li Baoyu, Dong Qin, Geshu Yao, Han Youhuan, Hun Shizhi, and Xin Jinggao each have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi's subordinate generals — Li Huai'guang, Pugu Huai'en, Tian Shegong, Li Baoyu, Dong Qin, Geshu Yao, Han Youhuan, Hun Shizhi, and Xin Jinggao — each have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 若荔非元禮、郝廷玉、李國臣、白孝德、張伯儀、白元光、陳利貞、侯仲莊、柏良器，皆章章可稱列者，附次左方。

translations.literal: As for Lifei Yuanli, Hao Tingyu, Li Guochen, Bai Xiaode, Zhang Boyi, Bai Yuanguang, Chen Lizhen, Hou Zhongzhuang, and Bai Liangqi — all clearly worthy of being ranked — their accounts are appended below at left.
translations.idiomatic: Lifei Yuanli, Hao Tingyu, Li Guochen, Bai Xiaode, Zhang Boyi, Bai Yuanguang, Chen Lizhen, Hou Zhongzhuang, and Bai Liangqi — all men of clear distinction — are recorded in the appended accounts that follow.

sentences.zh: 附 荔非元禮

translations.literal: Appended: Lifei Yuanli
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Lifei Yuanli

sentences.zh: 荔非元禮起裨將，累兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Lifei Yuanli rose from lieutenant general and was repeatedly given concurrent appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Lifei Yuanli began as a lieutenant general and was repeatedly given concurrent appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 光弼守河陽，周摯攻北城，光弼方壁中潬，摯聞，並兵從光弼。

translations.literal: Guangbi defended Heyang; Zhou Zhi attacked the north wall. Guangbi was then in the inner moat fort within the walls; Zhi heard of it and combined his forces to turn on Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Guangbi held Heyang, Zhou Zhi attacked the north wall. Guangbi was then commanding from the inner moat fort; when Zhi learned of this, he united his forces and turned against Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 光弼使元禮守羊馬城，植小旗城東北隅，望摯軍。

translations.literal: Guangbi had Yuanli hold the livestock enclosure wall, planted a small flag at the northeast corner of the city, and watched Zhi's army.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi ordered Yuanli to hold the livestock enclosure wall, set a small flag at the city's northeast corner, and watch Zhou Zhi's army from there.

sentences.zh: 摯恃眾，直逼城，以車千乘載木鵝橦車，麾兵填塹，八道並進。

translations.literal: Zhi relied on his numbers, pressed straight to the wall, used a thousand carts to carry wooden rams and covered assault wagons, commanded troops to fill the moat, and advanced on eight routes at once.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in his numbers, Zhi pressed straight up to the wall with a thousand carts bearing wooden rams and covered assault wagons, ordered his men to fill the moat, and advanced along eight routes at once.

sentences.zh: 光弼諭元禮曰：「中丞視賊過兵不顧，何也？」

translations.literal: Guangbi instructed Yuanli, saying, "Vice Censor, you watch the bandits pass by without heeding the troops — why?
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi sent word to Yuanli: "Vice Censor, you see the enemy pass and pay no attention to your troops — why?

sentences.zh: 報曰：「公欲守邪？

translations.literal: He replied, "Does the Lord wish to defend?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli replied, "Do you mean to defend, my lord?

sentences.zh: 戰歟？」

translations.literal: Or fight?"
translations.idiomatic: Or to fight?"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「戰。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "Fight."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "Fight."

sentences.zh: 曰：「方戰，賊為我實塹，復何怪？」

translations.literal: He said, "When fighting, the bandits fill the moat for us — what is there to wonder at?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli said, "If we are to fight, the enemy is filling the moat for us — what is strange about that?"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「吾慮不及此，公勉之。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said, "My thought did not reach this far — exert yourself, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "I had not thought that far ahead. Do your utmost, sir."

sentences.zh: 元禮遂出戰，摯軍小卻。

translations.literal: Yuanli then went out to battle; Zhi's army fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli then sallied forth; Zhou Zhi's army gave ground a little.

sentences.zh: 元禮以敵堅，未可以馳，還軍示弱，怠其意。

translations.literal: Yuanli, judging the enemy firm and not yet fit for a charge, withdrew his army to show weakness and slacken their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the enemy line too solid for a cavalry charge, Yuanli pulled his troops back to feign weakness and lull the enemy.

sentences.zh: 光弼怒，使召元禮，欲按軍法。

translations.literal: Guangbi grew angry, sent to summon Yuanli, and intended to punish him under military law.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi grew angry, sent for Yuanli, and meant to punish him under military law.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「方戰，不及往，請破賊以見。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Battle is underway; I cannot come — allow me to break the bandits and then appear before you.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli answered, "The battle is still on — I cannot leave now. Let me break the enemy first, and then I will come before you.

sentences.zh: 因休柵中，良久，顧麾下曰：「向公來召，殆欲斬我。

translations.literal: He therefore rested within the palisade; after a long while he turned to his followers and said, "When the Lord summoned me just now, he likely meant to behead me.
translations.idiomatic: He rested inside the palisade. After a long while he turned to his men and said, "When the commander sent for me just now, he probably meant to cut off my head.

sentences.zh: 鬥死有名，無庸受戮。」

translations.literal: To die fighting brings renown; there is no need to accept execution."
translations.idiomatic: Better to die fighting and win a name than to submit to the blade."

sentences.zh: 乃下馬持刀，瞋目直前，銳士堵而進，左右奮擊，一當數人，斬賊數百首，摯遁去。

translations.literal: He then dismounted, took blade in hand, glared and pressed straight forward; elite soldiers massed and advanced, striking fiercely on both flanks, each man matching several foes, beheading several hundred bandits; Zhi fled.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted, drew his blade, glared, and charged straight ahead. His crack troops closed ranks and pressed forward, striking on both flanks — each man took on several foes and cut down hundreds of the enemy. Zhou Zhi fled.

sentences.zh: 以功累遷驃騎大將軍、懷州刺史，知鎮西、北庭行營節度使。

translations.literal: For merit he was repeatedly promoted to Flying-Cavalry Grand General, Prefect of Huaizhou, and acting Military Governor of the Zhenxi and Beiting field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he rose through successive promotions to Flying-Cavalry Grand General and prefect of Huaizhou, with acting authority over the Zhenxi and Beiting field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，光弼進收洛陽，軍敗，元禮徙軍翼成，為麾下所害。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, Guangbi advanced to recover Luoyang; the army was defeated; Yuanli moved his army to Yicheng and was killed by his own subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shangyuan, when Guangbi advanced to retake Luoyang and the army was defeated, Yuanli withdrew his forces to Yicheng, where his own subordinates killed him.

sentences.zh: 附 郝廷玉

translations.literal: Appended: Hao Tingyu
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Hao Tingyu

sentences.zh: 郝廷玉驍勇善格鬥，為光弼愛將。

translations.literal: Hao Tingyu was fierce and brave, skilled at close combat, and was Guangbi's favored general.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Tingyu was fierce in battle and skilled at hand-to-hand fighting; he was one of Li Guangbi's favorite generals.

sentences.zh: 及保河陽，禽徐璜玉，功為多。
