translations.literal: When defending Heyang, he captured Xu Huangyu; his merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When Heyang was held, he captured Xu Huangyu and contributed more to the victory than any other officer.

sentences.zh: 累封安邊郡王，授神策將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Prince of Anbian Commandery and appointed General of the Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Prince of Anbian and appointed a general of the Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃犯京畿，與馬璘屯中渭橋。

translations.literal: When Tibetans raided the capital region, he encamped with Ma Lin at Central Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans threatened the capital region, he encamped with Ma Lin at Central Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 它日，魚朝恩聞其善佈陣，請觀之。

translations.literal: On another day, Yu Chaoen heard he was skilled at deploying formations and asked to observe.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, Yu Chaoen heard that he was skilled at deploying formations and asked to watch a drill.

sentences.zh: 廷玉申號令，鳴鼓角，部伍坐作進退若一。

translations.literal: Tingyu issued commands, sounded drums and horns, and the ranks sat, rose, advanced, and retreated as one.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu issued his commands; drums and horns sounded, and the ranks sat, rose, advanced, and retreated in perfect unison.

sentences.zh: 朝恩歎曰：「吾處兵間久，今始識訓練法。」

translations.literal: Chaoen sighed and said, "I have long been among troops, yet only now do I recognize the method of training.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen sighed and said, "I have spent my life among soldiers, yet only today do I see what real training looks like.

sentences.zh: 廷玉惻然曰：「此臨淮王遺法也。

translations.literal: Tingyu said sadly, "This is the legacy method of the Prince of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu said sadly, "This is the legacy of the Prince of Huai.

sentences.zh: 王善禦軍，賞當功，罰適過，每校旗，不如令者輒斬。

translations.literal: The Prince was skilled at commanding troops: rewards matched merit, punishments matched fault; at each flag inspection, whoever failed the command was immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince knew how to command an army — rewards matched merit and punishments matched fault. At every flag inspection, any man who failed to obey was beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 由是人皆自效，而赴蹈馳突，心破膽裂。

translations.literal: Therefore every man exerted himself; they rushed forward and charged, hearts broken and gall split.
translations.idiomatic: Because of that, every man gave his utmost; they charged and fought with hearts set on death and courage that shattered the enemy's nerve.

sentences.zh: 自臨淮歿，無復校旗事，此安足賞哉？」

translations.literal: Since the Prince of Huai died, there have been no more flag inspections — how can this be worth praise?"
translations.idiomatic: Since the Prince of Huai died, no one has held flag inspections anymore. What is there to admire in this?"

sentences.zh: 累為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly made Prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly as prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 附 李國臣

translations.literal: Appended: Li Guochen
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Li Guochen

sentences.zh: 李國臣，河西人，本姓安。

translations.literal: Li Guochen was a man of Hexi; his original surname was An.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guochen was a native of Hexi; his original surname was An.

sentences.zh: 力能抉關，以折沖從收魚海五城，遷中郎將。

translations.literal: His strength could wrench gates open; as a vanguard officer he followed in recovering the five cities of Yuhai and was promoted to Palace Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Strong enough to wrench open city gates, he served as a vanguard officer in the recovery of the five cities of Yuhai and was promoted to palace guard general.

sentences.zh: 後為朔方將，積勞擢雲麾大將軍，賜姓李。

translations.literal: Later he became a Shuofang general; for accumulated service he was promoted to Cloud-Banner Grand General and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as a Shuofang general. For long and meritorious service he was promoted to Cloud-Banner Grand General and granted the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 從光弼守河陽，累封臨川郡王。

translations.literal: Following Guangbi in defending Heyang, he was repeatedly enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Guangbi at Heyang, he was repeatedly enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 大曆八年，為鹽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, he became Prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dali he was appointed prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃敗渾瑊于黃菩原，將略汧、隴，國臣謂人曰：「虜乘勝，必擾京師，我趨秦原，彼當反顧。」

translations.literal: Tibetans defeated Hun Jian at Huangpuyuan and were about to strike Qian and Long; Guochen told others, "The barbarians, riding victory, will surely disturb the capital — if we hurry toward Qinyuan, they will look back.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans defeated Hun Jian at Huangpuyuan and prepared to advance into Qian and Long, Guochen told his officers, "The enemy, emboldened by victory, will surely threaten the capital. If we strike toward Qinyuan, they will have to turn back.

sentences.zh: 乃引兵登安樂山，鳴鼓而西，日行三十里。

translations.literal: He therefore led troops up Mount Anle, sounded drums, and marched west thirty li a day.
translations.idiomatic: He led his troops up Mount Anle, beat the drums, and marched west at thirty li a day.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃聞之，自百里城回軍，逾險，瑊因擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Tibetans heard of it, turned their army back from Bailicheng, crossed difficult terrain, and Jian therefore struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans heard of this, they wheeled about at Bailicheng and withdrew over difficult ground; Hun Jian took advantage and routed them.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Grand Protector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously appointed Grand Protector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 附 白孝德

translations.literal: Appended: Bai Xiaode
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Bai Xiaode

sentences.zh: 白孝德，安西人，事光弼為偏裨。

translations.literal: Bai Xiaode was a man of Anxi; he served Guangbi as a lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Xiaode was a native of Anxi who served Li Guangbi as a lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 史思明攻河陽，使驍將劉龍仙以騎五十挑戰，加右足馬鬣上，嫚罵光弼。

translations.literal: Shi Siming attacked Heyang and sent the fierce general Liu Longxian with fifty horsemen to challenge; placing his right foot on the horse's mane, he reviled Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming attacked Heyang, he sent the fierce general Liu Longxian with fifty horsemen to challenge the defenders. Longxian stood with his right foot on his horse's mane and hurled insults at Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 光弼登城顧諸將曰：「孰能取是賊？」

translations.literal: Guangbi mounted the wall, looked at the generals, and said, "Who can take this bandit?
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi climbed the wall, looked at his generals, and asked, "Who can bring down this enemy?

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩請行，光弼曰：「是非大將所宜。」

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en requested to go; Guangbi said, "This is not what a grand general should do."
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en volunteered, but Guangbi said, "This is not work for a chief general."

sentences.zh: 左右以孝德對。

translations.literal: Those beside him named Xiaode.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him suggested Xiaode.

sentences.zh: 召問所須幾兵，對曰：「願出五十騎，見可而進，大軍鼓噪以張吾氣，足矣。」

translations.literal: Summoned and asked how many troops he needed, he replied, "I wish to go out with fifty horsemen, advance when I see an opening, and let the main army raise a clamor to swell our spirit — that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned and asked how many men he needed, Xiaode replied, "Give me fifty horsemen. I will advance when I see an opening, and let the main army raise a clamor to hearten us — that will be enough.

sentences.zh: 光弼撫其背遣之。

translations.literal: Guangbi patted his back and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi clapped him on the back and sent him out.

sentences.zh: 孝德擁二矛，策馬絕河，半濟，懷恩賀曰：「事克矣。

translations.literal: Xiaode grasped two spears, spurred his horse across the river; halfway across, Huai'en congratulated him, saying, "The affair is won.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode took up two spears and spurred his horse across the river. When he was halfway over, Huai'en cried, "The thing is as good as done!

sentences.zh: 其攬轡便辟，可萬全者。」

translations.literal: The way he gathers the reins with skill — he can be perfectly secure.
translations.idiomatic: See how easily he handles the reins — nothing can go wrong now.

sentences.zh: 龍仙見，易之，不為動。

translations.literal: Longxian saw him, treated him lightly, and did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Longxian saw him coming and took him lightly, showing no alarm.

sentences.zh: 將至，若引避然，孝德振手止之曰：「侍中使致辭，無它。」

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive, as if to withdraw, Xiaode waved his hand to stop him and said, "The Palace Attendant sends me to deliver a message — nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaode drew near as if to pass by, he raised his hand to stop Longxian and said, "The Palace Attendant sends me with a message — nothing more.

sentences.zh: 與語須之，瞋目曰：「賊識我乎？

translations.literal: After speaking with him a while, he glared and said, "Bandit, do you know me?
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged words for a moment; then Xiaode glared and said, "Do you know who I am, you wretch?

sentences.zh: 我，白孝德也。」

translations.literal: I am Bai Xiaode."
translations.idiomatic: I am Bai Xiaode."

sentences.zh: 龍仙罵之，乃躍馬前搏，城上因大噪，五十騎繼進，龍仙環堤走，追斬其首以還。

translations.literal: Longxian cursed him; Xiaode then leapt his horse forward to grapple; the men on the wall raised a great clamor; fifty horsemen followed in; Longxian fled around the embankment; they pursued and beheaded him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Longxian cursed him. Xiaode spurred his horse forward to grapple. The men on the wall raised a great shout, fifty horsemen charged after him, and Longxian fled along the embankment. They ran him down, cut off his head, and returned.

sentences.zh: 後累功至北庭行營節度使，徙邠寧。

translations.literal: Later, for accumulated merit he reached Military Governor of the Beiting field headquarters and was transferred to Binning.
translations.idiomatic: For later achievements he rose to military governor of the Beiting field headquarters and was then transferred to Binning.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩引吐蕃兵入寇，孝德擊敗之。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en led Tibetan troops in invasion; Xiaode defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en led Tibetan troops in an invasion, Xiaode defeated them.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，吐蕃、回紇圍涇陽，郭子儀說回紇約盟，吐蕃退走，子儀使渾瑊以兵五千出奉天，命孝德應之，大戰赤沙烽，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai, Tibetans and Uyghurs besieged Jingyang; Guo Ziyi persuaded the Uyghurs to covenant; the Tibetans withdrew; Ziyi sent Hun Jian with five thousand troops out from Fengtian and ordered Xiaode to respond; they fought a great battle at Chisha Beacon, beheading and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongtai reign, Tibetans and Uyghurs besieged Jingyang. Guo Ziyi persuaded the Uyghurs to make peace, and the Tibetans withdrew. Ziyi sent Hun Jian with five thousand men out from Fengtian and ordered Xiaode to join him. At Chisha Beacon they fought a great battle and killed or captured a great number of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 累封昌化郡王，曆太子少傅。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Prince of Changhua Commandery and served as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Prince of Changhua and served as junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 建中元年卒，贈太保。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Jianzhong; posthumously made Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jianzhong and was posthumously appointed Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 附 張伯儀

translations.literal: Appended: Zhang Boyi
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Zhang Boyi

sentences.zh: 張伯儀，魏州人，以戰功隸光弼軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Boyi was a man of Weizhou; for battle merit he was attached to Guangbi's army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Boyi was a native of Weizhou who, for his achievements in battle, was assigned to Li Guangbi's army.

sentences.zh: 浙賊袁晁反，使伯儀討平之，功第一，擢睦州刺史。

translations.literal: The Zhe bandit Yuan Chao rebelled; Boyi was sent to suppress and pacify him; his merit ranked first, and he was promoted to Prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhe rebel Yuan Chao rose in revolt, Boyi was sent to suppress him. His achievement ranked first, and he was promoted to prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 後為江陵節度使。

translations.literal: Later he became Military Governor of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as military governor of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 樸厚不知書，然推誠遇人，軍中畏肅，民亦便之。

translations.literal: Plain and honest, he did not know books, yet he treated people with sincere trust; the army feared and respected him, and the people also found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and honest, he was no scholar, yet he dealt with people in good faith. His troops feared and respected him, and the common people found him easy to live under.

sentences.zh: 李希烈反，詔與賈耽、張獻甫收安州。

translations.literal: Li Xilie rebelled; an edict ordered him, together with Jia Dan and Zhang Xianfu, to recover Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, an edict ordered Boyi, together with Jia Dan and Zhang Xianfu, to recover Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 戰不利，伯儀中流矢，師卻，失所持節。

translations.literal: The battle went badly; Boyi was struck by a flying arrow; the army withdrew; he lost the tally he carried.
translations.idiomatic: The battle went badly. Boyi was struck by an arrow, the army fell back, and he lost the command tally he carried.

sentences.zh: 賊追及，奮刀以禦之，兩刃相向不得下，會救至，免。

translations.literal: Bandits caught up; he swung his blade to fend them off; the two edges faced each other and could not descend; rescue arrived, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy caught up with him. He swung his blade to fend them off, and the two edges locked so that neither could strike home. Relief arrived just in time, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 至漢水，拿野人船以達沔州。

translations.literal: Reaching the Han River, he seized local people's boats to reach Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Han River, he commandeered local boats and crossed to Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 潰兵至江陵，哭于廷，伯儀妻勞勉，出其家帛給之，乃定。

translations.literal: Routed troops reached Jiangling and wept in the hall; Boyi's wife comforted and encouraged them, brought out the family's silk to give them, and only then were they settled.
translations.idiomatic: Routed soldiers reached Jiangling and wept in the hall. Boyi's wife comforted and encouraged them and gave out the family's silk to supply them; only then did the men settle down.

sentences.zh: 伯儀收散卒還。

translations.literal: Boyi gathered scattered soldiers and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi gathered the scattered troops and returned.

sentences.zh: 久之，除右龍武統軍。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was appointed Commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Grand Protector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously appointed Grand Protector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 既請諡，博士李吉甫議以「中興三十年而兵未戢者，將帥養寇籓身也。

translations.literal: When a posthumous title was requested, Academician Li Jifu argued that "in the thirty years since the restoration, arms have not been stilled because generals nurture the bandits to enrich themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When a posthumous title was requested, Academician Li Jifu argued that "for thirty years since the restoration, war has never truly ended because commanders have nurtured the enemy to enrich themselves.

sentences.zh: 若以亡敗為戒，則總干戈者必圖萬全，而不決戰。

translations.literal: If defeat is taken as a warning, then those who command arms will surely seek perfect safety and will not decide battle.
translations.idiomatic: If defeat alone is held up as a warning, then every man who commands an army will seek perfect safety and refuse to risk decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 若伯儀雖敗，而其忠可錄。」

translations.literal: Boyi, though defeated, had loyalty worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi was defeated, yet his loyalty deserves to be remembered.

sentences.zh: 遂諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Therefore the posthumous title was Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous title Respectful was therefore granted.

sentences.zh: 附 白元光

translations.literal: Appended: Bai Yuanguang
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Bai Yuanguang

sentences.zh: 白元光，字元光，其先突厥人。

translations.literal: Bai Yuanguang, courtesy name Yuanguang, his ancestors were Turkic people.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yuanguang, whose courtesy name was also Yuanguang, was of Turkic descent.

sentences.zh: 父道生，曆寧、朔州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Daosheng successively served as Prefect of Ning and Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daosheng had served successively as prefect of Ning and Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 元光初隸本軍，補節度先鋒。

translations.literal: Yuanguang at first was attached to the native army and was appointed vanguard of the military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang first served in the local army and was appointed vanguard of the military governorship.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，詔徙朔方兵東討，元光領所部結義營，長驅從光弼出土門。

translations.literal: An Lushan rebelled; an edict moved Shuofang troops east to punish the rebellion; Yuanguang led his Jieyi Camp unit in a long drive, following Guangbi out through Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, an edict ordered Shuofang troops east to suppress the rebellion. Yuanguang led his Jieyi Camp in a long march, following Guangbi out through Tumen.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子詹事，封南陽郡王，為兩都遊弈使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Household Steward of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang Commandery, and made Patrolling Commissioner of the Two Capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to household steward of the heir apparent, was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang, and was appointed patrolling commissioner of the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 長安平，率兵清宮，進擊餘寇，身被數創，肅宗躬為傅藥。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, he led troops to clear the palace, advanced to attack remaining bandits, received several wounds on his body, and Emperor Suzong personally applied medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an was recovered, he led troops to secure the palace and pressed the attack against remaining rebels. He received several wounds, and Emperor Suzong personally applied medicine to him.

sentences.zh: 轉衛尉卿，兼朔方先鋒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Guard and concurrently served as Shuofang vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of the guard and concurrently served as Shuofang vanguard.

sentences.zh: 史思明攻河陽，光弼召主騎軍。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming attacked Heyang, Guangbi summoned him to command the cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming attacked Heyang, Guangbi summoned him to take command of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 其後曆靈武留後、定遠城使。

translations.literal: Afterward he successively served as Lingwu regent and commissioner of Dingyuan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He later served successively as regent of Lingwu and commissioner of Dingyuan Fort.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年卒，贈越州都督。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Zhenyuan; posthumously made Protector-General of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhenyuan and was posthumously appointed protector-general of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 附 陳利貞

translations.literal: Appended: Chen Lizhen
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Chen Lizhen

sentences.zh: 陳利貞，幽州范陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Lizhen was a man of Fanyang in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lizhen was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為平盧將，安祿山亂，從光弼軍河南。

translations.literal: At first he was a Pinglu officer; when An Lushan rebelled he followed Guangbi's army to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an officer in Pinglu. When An Lushan rebelled, he followed Li Guangbi's army into Henan.

sentences.zh: 張巡被圍睢陽也，光弼遣郝廷玉及利貞救之，輕騎出入，廷玉稱為勝己，以子妻之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xun was besieged at Suiyang, Guangbi sent Hao Tingyu and Lizhen to relieve him; with light cavalry they went in and out; Tingyu said Lizhen surpassed himself and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xun was besieged at Suiyang, Guangbi sent Hao Tingyu and Chen Lizhen to his relief. Riding light cavalry in and out of the siege, Lizhen distinguished himself so greatly that Tingyu declared him his superior and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 及歸，薦於光弼，自行間累遷檢校太子賓客，封靜戎郡王。

translations.literal: On returning he was recommended to Guangbi; from the ranks he was promoted through posts to Acting Crown Prince's Guest and enfeoffed as Prince of Jingrong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was recommended to Guangbi and rose through the ranks to acting Crown Prince's Guest, being created Prince of Jingrong.

sentences.zh: 李希烈叛，詔哥舒曜東討，利貞為前鋒，次郟城。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, an edict ordered Geshu Yao east to suppress him; Lizhen was vanguard and halted at Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, an edict ordered Geshu Yao east to suppress him. Lizhen served as vanguard and encamped at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 賊眾大集，利貞出奇兵五百，橫搗其右，賊鋒詘，數月不敢前。

translations.literal: Rebel forces massed greatly; Lizhen sent five hundred picked troops to strike their right flank; the rebel spearhead bent; for months they did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel forces massed in strength, Lizhen sent five hundred picked troops to strike their right flank. The enemy vanguard faltered and for months dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 及希烈攻曜襄城，利貞登陴捍守，七十日未嘗櫛沐，非議事不下城。

translations.literal: When Xilie attacked Yao at Xiangcheng, Lizhen mounted the battlements to defend; for seventy days he never combed or bathed; unless for council he did not leave the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie attacked Geshu Yao at Xiangcheng, Lizhen mounted the walls to defend the city. For seventy days he neither combed his hair nor bathed, and never left the ramparts except to discuss strategy.

sentences.zh: 硃泚反，利貞及張廷芝所統士皆幽、薊、河、隴人，故與廷芝合謀應泚，而利貞麾下亦從為亂。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, the troops Lizhen and Zhang Tingzhi commanded were all men of You, Ji, He, and Long, so they joined Tingzhi in plotting to answer Ci, and Lizhen's subordinates also followed in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, the troops under Chen Lizhen and Zhang Tingzhi were all men from You, Ji, He, and Long — frontier country — so they plotted together to join Zhu Ci, and Lizhen's own men followed them into mutiny.

sentences.zh: 夜半，難作，利貞拔劍當軍門，大呼曰：「欲過門者，先殺我！」

translations.literal: At midnight trouble broke out; Lizhen drew his sword and stood at the army gate, shouting, "Whoever wishes to pass this gate must kill me first!
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the mutiny erupted. Lizhen drew his sword and planted himself at the camp gate, shouting, "Whoever wishes to pass this gate must kill me first!

sentences.zh: 眾畏其勇，乃止。

translations.literal: The masses feared his courage and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The men, awed by his courage, held back.

sentences.zh: 廷芝出奔。

translations.literal: Tingzhi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingzhi fled.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，擢汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong commended him and promoted him to Defender of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong commended his conduct and appointed him defender of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，疽發首，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan an abscess broke out on his head and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan a carbuncle broke out on his head and he died.

sentences.zh: 遺觀察使崔縱書，自陳受國恩，恨不得死所雲。

translations.literal: He left a letter to Investigating Commissioner Cui Zong, stating himself that he had received the state's grace and regretted he had not found a place to die, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: He left a letter to Investigating Commissioner Cui Zong lamenting that he had received the state's grace yet had not found a place to die for it.

sentences.zh: 附 侯仲莊

translations.literal: Appended: Hou Zhongzhuang
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Hou Zhongzhuang

sentences.zh: 侯仲莊，字仲莊，蔚州人。

translations.literal: Hou Zhongzhuang, style name Zhongzhuang, was a man of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhongzhuang, whose style name was the same as his given name, was a native of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為光弼先鋒，授忠武將軍。

translations.literal: He served as Guangbi's vanguard and was appointed Loyal Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Li Guangbi's vanguard and was appointed Loyal Martial General.

sentences.zh: 禽安太清有功，累加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: For merit in capturing An Taiqing he was repeatedly promoted to Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing An Taiqing he was repeatedly promoted, eventually reaching Champion General.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩以朔方反，仲莊為都將，訓兵自守，號為「平射」，人畏其鋒。

translations.literal: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled with Shuofang, Zhongzhuang was commandery general, trained troops to hold themselves, and was called "Level Shot"; men feared his edge.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled from Shuofang, Zhongzhuang was a commandery general who drilled his troops for defense. Known as "Level Shot," he was feared for the sharpness of his attack.

sentences.zh: 懷恩敗，郭子儀代之，引為腹心。

translations.literal: When Huai'en was defeated, Guo Ziyi replaced him and drew Zhongzhuang into his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai'en's defeat, Guo Ziyi took his place and drew Zhongzhuang into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 封上谷郡王，為神策京西將。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Shanggu Commandery and made a Shence general of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Prince of Shanggu and appointed a Shence general on the western capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸奉天，遷左衛將軍，為防城使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong went to Fengtian, he was transferred to Left Guard General and made city defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian, Zhongzhuang was made Left Guard General and commissioner of city defense.

sentences.zh: 修壘堞，晝夜執戈徼巡。

translations.literal: He repaired ramparts and battlements and day and night bore arms on patrol.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the walls and battlements and patrolled day and night with weapon in hand.

sentences.zh: 從幸興元，殿軍駱谷，授防禦招收使。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Xingyuan, brought up the rear at Luogu Pass, and was appointed defense and recruitment commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Xingyuan, brought up the rear at Luogu Pass, and was appointed defense and recruitment commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝還都，復鎮奉天，幾二十年。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, he again garrisoned Fengtian for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, he garrisoned Fengtian again for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈洪州都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Military Governor of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously appointed Military Governor of Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 附 柏良器

translations.literal: Appended: Bai Liangqi
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Bai Liangqi

sentences.zh: 柏良器，字公亮，魏州人。

translations.literal: Bai Liangqi, style name Gongliang, was a man of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Liangqi, style name Gongliang, was a native of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父造，以獲嘉令死安祿山難。

translations.literal: His father Zao died in An Lushan's turmoil while serving as magistrate of Huojia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zao had died in An Lushan's rebellion while serving as magistrate of Huojia.

sentences.zh: 乃學擊劍，欲報賊。

translations.literal: He then studied swordsmanship, wishing to avenge himself on the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He took up swordsmanship, determined to avenge his father on the rebels.

sentences.zh: 父友王奐為光弼從事，見之曰：「爾額文似臨淮王，面黑子似顏平原，殆能立功。」

translations.literal: His father's friend Wang Huan served on Guangbi's staff; seeing him he said, "Your forehead markings resemble the Prince of Huai's, and the dark mole on your face resembles Yan the Plain's — you will likely achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: His father's friend Wang Huan, who served on Li Guangbi's staff, saw him and said, "The markings on your forehead resemble the Prince of Huai's, and the dark mole on your face resembles Yan Gaoqing's — you may well win great merit.

sentences.zh: 乃薦之光弼。

translations.literal: He then recommended him to Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang then recommended him to Li Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 授兵平山越，遷左武衛中郎將。

translations.literal: He was given troops to pacify the Shanyue, and was transferred to Central Captain of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was given troops to pacify the Shanyue and was promoted to Central Captain of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 以部兵隸浙西，豫平袁晁、方清。

translations.literal: With his unit attached to Zhexi, he took part in pacifying Yuan Chao and Fang Qing.
translations.idiomatic: His unit was attached to Zhexi, where he helped suppress the rebellions of Yuan Chao and Fang Qing.

sentences.zh: 其後潘獰虎、胡參分據小傷、蒸裏，又擊破之。

translations.literal: Afterward Pan Ninghu and Hu Can separately held Xiaoshang and Zhengli; he again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He later defeated Pan Ninghu and Hu Can, who had seized the districts of Xiaoshang and Zhengli.

sentences.zh: 是時年二十四，更戰陣六十二。

translations.literal: At that time he was twenty-four and had fought in sixty-two engagements.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was twenty-four and had fought in sixty-two engagements.

sentences.zh: 李希烈圍寧陵，遏水灌之，親令軍中明日拔城。

translations.literal: Li Xilie besieged Ningling, dammed water to flood it, and personally ordered the army to take the city tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie besieged Ningling, dammed the waters to flood it, and personally ordered his army to take the city the next day.

sentences.zh: 良器以救兵至，擇弩手善遊者，沿汴渠夜入，及旦，伏弩發，賊乘城者皆死。

translations.literal: Liangqi arrived with relief troops, chose crossbowmen skilled at swimming, entered by night along the Bian Canal, and at dawn hidden crossbows fired; rebels mounting the wall all died.
translations.idiomatic: Liangqi arrived with relief forces, selected crossbowmen who could swim, and sent them up the Bian Canal by night. At dawn their hidden crossbows fired, killing every rebel who had mounted the walls.

sentences.zh: 錄功封平原郡王，入為左神策軍大將軍、知軍事，圖形淩煙閣。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan Commandery; he entered court as Grand General of the Left Shence Army with control of army affairs; his portrait was placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he was created Prince of Pingyuan, appointed Grand General of the Left Shence Army with control of army affairs, and had his portrait placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 募材勇以代士卒市販者，中尉竇文場惡之，坐友人闌入，換右領軍衛。

translations.literal: He recruited the talented and brave to replace soldiers who peddled goods; Vice Director Dou Wenchang hated this and, on the pretext of a friend's unauthorized entry, transferred him to the Right Leading Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited able fighters to replace soldiers who spent their time trading in the markets. Vice Director Dou Wenchang resented this and, citing a friend's unauthorized entry, had him transferred to the Right Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 自是軍政皆中官專之。

translations.literal: From this time military government was monopolized by palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: From that point forward, military affairs fell entirely under eunuch control.

sentences.zh: 終左領軍衛大將軍，贈陝州大都督。

translations.literal: He ended as Grand General of the Left Leading Army Guard; posthumously made Grand Protector of Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Grand General of the Left Leading Army Guard and was posthumously appointed Grand Protector of Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子耆，別傳。

translations.literal: His son Qi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 附 烏承玼

translations.literal: Appended: Wu Chengci
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Wu Chengci

sentences.zh: 烏承玼，字德潤，張掖人。

translations.literal: Wu Chengci, style name Derun, was a man of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengci, style name Derun, was a native of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 開元中，與族兄承恩皆為平盧先鋒，沉勇而決，號「轅門二龍」。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he and his clan elder Chengen were both Pinglu vanguards, deep and brave and decisive, called "the Two Dragons of the Camp Gate."
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he and his clansman Chengen both served as Pinglu vanguards. Deeply brave and resolute, they were known as "the Two Dragons of the Camp Gate."

sentences.zh: 契丹可突于殺其王邵固降突厥，而奚亦亂，其王魯蘇挈族屬及邵固妻子自歸。

translations.literal: The Khitan Ketuyu killed their king Shaogu and surrendered to the Turks; the Xi also rebelled; their king Lusu led clansmen and Shaogu's wife and children to submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan leader Ketuyu killed his king Shaogu and submitted to the Turks. The Xi also rose in revolt, but their king Lusu led his clan and Shaogu's family to surrender to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，奚、契丹入寇，詔承玼擊之，破於捺祿山。

translations.literal: That year the Xi and Khitan raided; an edict ordered Chengci to strike them; he defeated them at Nalushan.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Xi and Khitan raided the frontier. An edict ordered Chengci against them, and he defeated them at Nalushan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，詔信安王禕率幽州長史趙含章進討，承玼請含章曰：「二虜固劇賊，前日戰而北，非畏我，乃誘我也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year an edict ordered Prince Xin'an Li Yi to lead Youzhou Chief Secretary Zhao Hanzhang in advance to attack; Chengci urged Hanzhang, saying, "The two barbarians are indeed fierce foes; their fighting northward the other day was not from fear of us but to lure us.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan, Prince Xin'an Li Yi was ordered to lead Youzhou Chief Secretary Zhao Hanzhang in an advance against the enemy. Chengci warned Hanzhang, "These two peoples are fierce enemies. Their retreat the other day was not from fear of us — it was a lure.

sentences.zh: 公宜畜銳以折其謀。」

translations.literal: You ought to store keen edge to break their design.
translations.idiomatic: You should conserve your strength to frustrate their scheme.

sentences.zh: 含章不信，戰白城，果大敗。

translations.literal: Hanzhang did not believe it; they fought at Bai City and were indeed routed.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhang did not believe him. They fought at Bai City and were routed.

sentences.zh: 承玼獨按隊出其右，斬首萬計，可突于奔北奚。

translations.literal: Chengci alone held his ranks and came out on their right, beheading on the order of ten thousand; Ketuyu fled north to the Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Chengci alone held his formation, struck from the enemy's right, and took more than ten thousand heads. Ketuyu fled north into Xi territory.

sentences.zh: 渤海大武藝與弟門藝戰國中，門藝來，詔與太僕卿金思蘭發范陽、新羅兵十萬討之，無功。

translations.literal: Bohai's Da Wuyi fought his younger brother Menyi within the state; Menyi came [to Tang]; an edict ordered him with Grand Master of the Stud Jin Silan to raise a hundred thousand troops from Fanyang and Silla to suppress Wuyi, without success.
translations.idiomatic: Da Wuyi of Bohai was at war with his younger brother Menyi within the kingdom. When Menyi fled to Tang, an edict ordered Chengci and Grand Master of the Stud Jin Silan to raise a hundred thousand men from Fanyang and Silla against Wuyi, but the campaign failed.

sentences.zh: 武藝遣客刺門藝於東都，引兵至馬都山，屠城邑。

translations.literal: Wuyi sent a guest to assassinate Menyi in the Eastern Capital and led troops to Madu Mountain, slaughtering cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi sent an assassin against Menyi in the Eastern Capital and led his army to Madu Mountain, slaughtering towns along the way.

sentences.zh: 承玼窒要路，塹以大石，亙四百里，虜不得入。

translations.literal: Chengci blocked the vital route and trenched it with great stones for four hundred li; the barbarians could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Chengci blocked the vital passes and barricaded them with great stones for four hundred li, keeping the enemy out.

sentences.zh: 於是流民得還，士少休，脫鎧而耕，歲省度支運錢。

translations.literal: Thus displaced people could return; soldiers rested somewhat, doffed armor and plowed, and each year the Ministry of Revenue saved transport money.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced civilians could return home, soldiers rested, doffed their armor to farm, and the Ministry of Revenue saved a fortune in transport costs each year.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒使史思明守范陽，思明恃兵強，為自固計。

translations.literal: An Qingxu sent Shi Siming to hold Fanyang; Siming relied on strong troops and made plans to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: An Qingxu sent Shi Siming to hold Fanyang. Siming, trusting in his army's strength, began scheming for his own security.

sentences.zh: 慶緒密遣阿史那承慶、安守忠就督事，且圖之。

translations.literal: Qingxu secretly sent Ashina Chengqing and An Shouzhong to oversee affairs and also to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu secretly sent Ashina Chengqing and An Shouzhong to oversee his affairs — and to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 承玼勸思明曰：「唐家中興，與天下更始，慶緒偷肆晷刻，公殆與俱亡。

translations.literal: Chengci urged Siming, saying, "The Tang house is restoring itself and renewing all under heaven with a fresh start; Qingxu steals his moments wantonly — you will likely perish together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengci urged Siming, "The Tang is restoring itself and renewing the realm. Qingxu steals his days — you will likely perish with him.

sentences.zh: 有如束身本朝，湔洗前汙，此反掌功耳。」

translations.literal: If you bind yourself to the native court and wash away former stains, this is merit that turns in the palm of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: If you submit to the Tang and wash away your former crimes, the achievement is as easy as turning your hand.

sentences.zh: 思明善之，斬承慶等，奉表聽命。

translations.literal: Siming approved this, beheaded Chengqing and the others, and submitted a memorial to obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Siming agreed, executed Chengqing and the others, and submitted a memorial of submission.

sentences.zh: 始，承恩為冀州刺史，失守，思明護送東都，故肅宗使自雲中趨幽州開說思明，與承玼謀投釁殺之，不克，死。

translations.literal: At first Chengen was Prefect of Ji; he lost his post; Siming escorted him to the Eastern Capital; therefore Emperor Suzong sent him from Yunzhong to hurry to Youzhou to open persuasion with Siming; he joined Chengci in plotting to seize an opening and kill him; they did not succeed and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chengen had been prefect of Ji but lost his post and was escorted by Siming to the Eastern Capital. Emperor Suzong therefore sent him from Yunzhong to Youzhou to persuade Siming to defect. He and Chengci plotted to kill Siming but failed, and Chengen died in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 承玼奔李光弼，表為冠軍將軍，封昌化郡王，為石嶺軍使。

translations.literal: Chengci fled to Li Guangbi; he was memorialized as Champion General, enfeoffed as Prince of Changhua Commandery, and made commander of the Shiling Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chengci fled to Li Guangbi, who recommended him as Champion General, created him Prince of Changhua, and appointed him commander of the Shiling Army.

sentences.zh: 王思禮為節度使，軍政倚辦焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Sili was military governor, military government relied on him for execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sili became military governor, he relied on Chengci for all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 久之，移疾還京師，卒，年九十六。

translations.literal: After a long time he pleaded illness and returned to the capital; he died at age ninety-six.
translations.idiomatic: After many years he pleaded illness and returned to the capital, where he died at the age of ninety-six.

sentences.zh: 子重胤，別傳。

translations.literal: His son Chongyin has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongyin is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：李光弼生戎虜之緒，沉鷙有守。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Li Guangbi was born of barbarian frontier stock, deep and fierce with self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal reads: Li Guangbi was born of frontier stock, yet he was deep, fierce, and self-disciplined.

sentences.zh: 遭祿山變，拔任兵柄，其策敵制勝不世出，賞信罰明，士卒爭奮，毅然有古良將風。

translations.literal: Meeting Lushan's upheaval, he was raised to wield the army's authority; his stratagems against the enemy and victories were unmatched in the age; rewards were trusted and punishments clear; soldiers strove forward; resolutely he had the bearing of ancient worthy generals.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion erupted, he was elevated to military command. His stratagems against the enemy were unmatched in his age. Rewards were sure and punishments clear; his soldiers fought with desperate zeal. He bore himself with the stern dignity of the great generals of old.

sentences.zh: 本夫終父喪不入妻室，位王公事繼母至孝，好讀班固《漢書》，異夫庸人武夫者。

translations.literal: Originally when his father's mourning ended he did not enter the wife's chamber; though ranked among kings and dukes he served his stepmother with utmost filiality; he loved reading Ban Gu's Book of Han — unlike the common run of martial men.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's mourning he would not enter his wife's chamber. Though he rose to the rank of king, he served his stepmother with the utmost filial devotion. He loved to read Ban Gu's History of the Han — a man utterly unlike the common run of soldiers.

sentences.zh: 及困於口舌，不能以忠自明，奄侍內構，遂陷嫌隙，謀就全安，而身益危，所謂工於料人而拙於謀己邪。

translations.literal: When trapped by words, he could not make his loyalty clear by himself; suddenly attendants fomented intrigue within, and he fell into suspicion and rifts; he sought complete safety yet his person grew still more imperiled — what is called skilled at measuring others yet clumsy at plotting for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when slander trapped him, he could not make his loyalty plain. Court attendants fomented intrigue against him, and he fell into suspicion and estrangement. Seeking only his own safety, he grew only more endangered — skilled at reading others, perhaps, but clumsy at reading himself.

sentences.zh: 方攘袂徇國，天下風靡；

translations.literal: Just as he rolled his sleeves to serve the state and all under heaven followed the wind;
translations.idiomatic: Just when he had rolled up his sleeves to serve the state and all the realm followed his lead,

sentences.zh: 一為遷延，而田神功等皆不受約束，卒以憂死。

translations.literal: once he delayed, Tian Shegong and the rest all refused restraint, and in the end he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: a single delay left Tian Shegong and others beyond his control, and in the end he died of grief.

sentences.zh: 功臣去就，可不慎邪？

translations.literal: A meritorious minister's coming and going — can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: How carefully must a great minister weigh his every move!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，光弼雖有不釋位之誅，然讒人為害，亦可畏矣，將時之不幸歟！

translations.literal: Alas! Though Guangbi had the fault of not relinquishing his post, yet slanderers did harm — this too is to be feared; was it perhaps the age's misfortune!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! Though Guangbi may be faulted for clinging to his command, the harm done by slanderers is fearful indeed. Was it not rather the misfortune of his times!
